items.summary: Model support & provider updates Added support for new Claude models including the Sonnet 4 and Opus 4 series (e.g., claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-opus-4-20250514) across various providers. The default sonnet and opus aliases were updated to these newer…
items.html:
Model support & provider updates

  • Added support for new Claude models including the Sonnet 4 and Opus 4 series (e.g., claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-opus-4-20250514) across various providers. The default sonnet and opus aliases were updated to these newer versions.
  • Added support for the vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-05-20 model.
  • Updated default OpenRouter models during onboarding to deepseek/deepseek-r1:free for the free tier and anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 for paid tiers.
  • Automatically refresh GitHub Copilot tokens when used as OpenAI API keys, by Lih Chen.

Core functionality improvements

  • Fixed an issue where files explicitly added via the command line were not correctly ignored if listed in .gitignore.
  • Improved automatic commit messages by providing more context during their generation, by wangboxue.
  • Fixed OpenRouter token cost calculation for improved accuracy.

Quality of life improvements

  • Improved OpenRouter model metadata handling by introducing a local cache, increasing reliability and performance.
  • Added shell tab completion for file path arguments (by saviour) and for --edit-format/--editor-edit-format options.
  • The /settings command now displays detailed metadata for active main, editor, and weak models.
  • Improved user language detection by correctly normalizing hyphenated language codes (e.g., en-US to en) and enhancing the validation of locale results.
  • Prevented aider from instructing the LLM to reply in 'C' or 'POSIX' when these are detected as the system locale.
  • Displayed a spinner with the model name when generating commit messages.
  • Bumped configargparse to 1.7.1 as 1.7 was pulled.

items.title: Aider v0.83.0
items.summary: Added support for gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06 models. Added support for qwen3-235b models. Added repo-map support for OCaml and OCaml interface files, by Andrey Popp. Added a spinner animation while waiting for the LLM to start streaming its response. Updated…
items.html:
• Added support for gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06 models.
  • Added support for qwen3-235b models.
  • Added repo-map support for OCaml and OCaml interface files, by Andrey Popp.
  • Added a spinner animation while waiting for the LLM to start streaming its response.
  • Updated the spinner animation to a Knight Rider style.
  • Introduced --attribute-co-authored-by option to add co-author trailer to commit messages, by Andrew Grigorev.
  • Updated Gemini model aliases (e.g., gemini, gemini-2.5-pro) to point to the 05-06 preview versions.
  • Marked Gemini 2.5 Pro preview models as overeager by default.
  • Commit message prompt specifies the user's language.
  • Updated the default weak model for Gemini 2.5 Pro models to gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-04-17.
  • Corrected gemini-2.5-pro-exp-03-25 model settings to reflect its lack of support for thinking_budget.
  • Ensured model-specific system prompt prefixes are placed on a new line before the main system prompt.
  • Added tracking of total tokens sent and received, now included in benchmark statistics.
  • Automatically fetch model parameters (context window, pricing) for OpenRouter models directly from their website, by Stefan Hladnik.
  • Enabled support for thinking_tokens and reasoning_effort parameters for OpenRouter models.
  • Improved cost calculation using litellm.completion_cost where available.
  • Added model settings for openrouter/google/gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25.
  • Added --disable-playwright flag to prevent Playwright installation prompts and usage, by Andrew Grigorev.
  • The aider scrape command-line tool will now use Playwright for web scraping if it is available, by Jon Keys.
  • Fixed linter command execution on Windows by adopting oslex for argument quoting, by Titusz Pan.
  • Improved cross-platform display of shell commands by using oslex for robust argument quoting, by Titusz Pan.
  • Improved /ask mode to instruct the LLM to elide unchanging code in its responses.
  • Ensured web scraping in the GUI also respects Playwright availability and the --disable-playwright flag.
  • Improved display of filenames in the prompt header using rich Text formatting.
  • Enabled reasoning_effort for Gemini 2.5 Flash models.
  • Added a --shell-completions argument to generate shell completion scripts (e.g., for bash, zsh).
  • Explicit --attribute-author or --attribute-committer flags now override the default behavior when --attribute-co-authored-by is used, allowing finer control over commit attribution, by Andrew Grigorev.
  • Fixed an issue where read-only status of files might not be preserved correctly by some commands (e.g. /drop after adding a read-only file).
  • The aider-args utility (or python -m aider.args) now defaults to printing a sample YAML configuration if no arguments are provided.
  • Displayed token count progress and the name of the file or identifier being processed during repo map updates.
  • Extended the waiting spinner to also show for non-streaming responses and further enhanced its animation with console width clipping, cursor hiding, and a more continuous appearance.
  • Dropped support for Python 3.9.
  • Aider wrote 55% of the code in this release.

items.html:
• Big upgrade in programming languages supported by adopting tree-sitter-language-pack.

    • 130 new languages with linter support.
    • 20 new languages with repo-map support.

  • Added /think-tokens command to set thinking token budget with support for human-readable formats (8k, 10.5k, 0.5M).

  • Added /reasoning-effort command to control model reasoning level.

  • The /think-tokens and /reasoning-effort commands display current settings when called without arguments.

  • Display of thinking token budget and reasoning effort in model information.

  • Changed --thinking-tokens argument to accept string values with human-readable formats.

  • Added --auto-accept-architect flag (default: true) to automatically accept changes from architect coder format without confirmation.

  • Added support for cohere_chat/command-a-03-2025 and gemini/gemma-3-27b-it

  • The bare /drop command now preserves original read-only files provided via args.read.

  • Fixed a bug where default model would be set by deprecated --shortcut switches even when already specified in the command line.

  • Improved AutoCompleter to require 3 characters for autocompletion to reduce noise.

  • Fixed handling of JSONDecodeError when loading model cache file.

  • Fixed handling of GitCommandError when retrieving git user configuration.

  • Added ignore_permission_denied option to file watcher to prevent errors when accessing restricted files, by Yutaka Matsubara.

items.html:
• Improved support for thinking/reasoning models:

    • Added --thinking-tokens CLI option to control token budget for models that support thinking.
    • Display thinking/reasoning content from LLMs which return it.
    • Enhanced handling of reasoning tags to better clean up model responses.
    • Added deprecation warning for remove_reasoning setting, now replaced by reasoning_tag.

  • Aider will notify you when it's completed the last request and needs your input:

    • Added notifications when LLM responses are ready with --notifications flag.
    • Specify desktop notification command with --notifications-command.

  • Added/improved support for many models/providers:

    • Added support for QWQ 32B.
    • Support for DeepSeek V3 free on OpenRouter: --model openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-chat:free.
    • Added support for Claude 3.7 Sonnet models on OpenRouter, Bedrock and Vertex AI.
    • Updated default model to Claude 3.7 Sonnet on OpenRouter.
    • Added support for GPT-4.5-preview model.
    • Added support for Claude 3.7 Sonnet:beta on OpenRouter.
    • Added support for openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet
    • Fixed weak_model_name patterns to match main model name patterns for some models.

  • Switch to tree-sitter-language-pack for tree sitter support.

  • Improved error handling for EOF (Ctrl+D) in user input prompts.

  • Added helper function to ensure hex color values have a # prefix.

  • Fixed handling of Git errors when reading staged files.

  • Improved SSL verification control for model information requests.

  • Improved empty LLM response handling with clearer warning messages.

  • Fixed Git identity retrieval to respect global configuration, by Akira Komamura.

  • Offer to install dependencies for Bedrock and Vertex AI models.

  • Deprecated model shortcut args (like --4o, --opus) in favor of the --model flag.

• Dynamically changes the Ollama context window to hold the current chat.
  • Better support for o3-mini, DeepSeek V3 & R1, o1-mini, o1 via secondary API providers.
  • Remove <think> tags from R1 responses for commit messages (and other weak model uses).
  • Can now specify use_temperature: <float> in model settings, not just true/false.
  • The full docker container now includes boto3 for Bedrock.
  • Docker containers now set HOME=/app which is the normal project mount-point, to persist ~/.aider.
  • Bugfix to prevent creating incorrect filenames like python, php, etc.
  • Bugfix for --timeout
  • Bugfix so that /model now correctly reports that the weak model is not changed.
  • Bugfix so that multi-line mode persists through ^C at confirmation prompts.
  • Watch files now fully ignores top-level directories named in ignore files, to reduce the chance of hitting OS watch limits. Helpful to ignore giant subtrees like node_modules.
  • Fast startup with more providers and when model metadata provided in local files.
  • Improved .gitignore handling:
    • Honor ignores already in effect regardless of how they've been configured.
    • Check for .env only when the file exists.
  • Yes/No prompts now accept All/Skip as alias for Y/N even when not processing a group of confirmations.

items.html:
Claude Squad v1.0.0

Claude Squad is a terminal app lets you manage multiple Claude Code (and other local agents like Aider) instances across separate workspaces, so you can tackle multiple tasks at once.

  • Run tasks in the background (with yolo/auto-accept mode)
  • Control all instances and tasks from one terminal window
  • Review changes before applying, checkout before pushing
  • Isolated git workspaces per task—no more conflicts!

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 12, 2026
items.summary: App + chat connectors: Deel and Retool Deel lets apps read and update your company's contracts, people, timesheets, and time off, and read its payments. Use it for team directories, timesheet approval queues, and payroll reports. Retool lets apps manage the…
items.html:
App + chat connectors: Deel and Retool

Deel lets apps read and update your company's contracts, people, timesheets, and time off, and read its payments. Use it for team directories, timesheet approval queues, and payroll reports.

Retool lets apps manage the members, groups, and permissions of your Retool organization and embed your existing Retool apps. Use it for team administration dashboards, access reviews, and portals that bring your Retool tools together.

Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Review critical security findings before you publish

When you publish a project that uses the built-in backend and has unresolved critical security findings, Lovable now asks you to review them first. You can open them in the Security view, publish anyway, or ask Lovable to fix them all in one request, which uses one of your free fixes.

Fix security findings from the project chat

You can now fix security findings from the project chat. When your project has open critical findings or warnings, a notice above the chat input shows how many. Select Fix all to send them to Lovable in one request, which uses one of your free fixes.

Get an alert when your run usage rises sharply

On paid plans, workspace admins and owners now get an email and an in-app notification when the workspace's daily run usage rises sharply compared with the previous 7 days. The alert does not block usage.

See the published commit in audit logs

On Enterprise plans, each publishing event in your workspace's audit logs now records the commit that was published, so you can trace a published app back to its code. Expand the event to see it.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 11, 2026
items.summary: Hand recurring work to Lovable with automations Automations let Lovable take care of the work you repeat, such as a morning check of your published sites, a weekly summary of new signups, or a Friday list of the oldest items in your backlog. Ask for one in…
items.html:
Hand recurring work to Lovable with automations

Automations let Lovable take care of the work you repeat, such as a morning check of your published sites, a weekly summary of new signups, or a Friday list of the oldest items in your backlog. Ask for one in Chats and say how often, and Lovable posts what it finds there. Automations are available on Free, Pro, and Business plans, and each run is chat usage.

Invitations are no longer accepted automatically

You now accept each invitation to a workspace or a project yourself, from the email or your Inbox. Auto-accept invitations has been removed from your account settings.

Edit images in Chats

Images you open in Chats now have the same image editing toolbar as a project's Files tab, so you can describe edits, erase, resize, or turn an image into a short video. Lovable saves each edit as a new version of the image.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 10, 2026
items.summary: See when your monthly credits renew On Pro and Business plans, the credit bar in your workspace menu now shows the date your monthly credits renew next, whether you pay monthly or annually. Add personal skills You can now add personal skills, playbooks that…
items.html:
See when your monthly credits renew

On Pro and Business plans, the credit bar in your workspace menu now shows the date your monthly credits renew next, whether you pay monthly or annually.

Add personal skills

You can now add personal skills, playbooks that only you can use, with a separate set in each workspace. Lovable applies one when a task matches it. Add them in your account settings, or ask Lovable in a project chat to write one.

Set personal instructions

You can now set personal instructions, rules and preferences that Lovable follows in every project you open in a workspace. Your teammates never see them. Set them in your account settings, separately for each workspace.

Lovable keeps a separate personal memory in each workspace

Personal memory, what Lovable remembers about how you like to work, is now separate in each workspace, so what Lovable learns about you in one workspace does not carry over to the others. Personal memory has also moved to your account settings, where you pick a workspace to see its memory or disable it.

Require two-factor authentication from external collaborators

Enterprise workspace admins and owners can now require two-factor authentication from external collaborators only, by choosing External collaborators. You can choose it even when Enforce SSO is enabled.

Update several connectors at once

Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans can now set the availability of several connectors in one step in the Connectors admin settings, which makes it quick to keep only the connectors your team needs.

Redesigned Connectors catalog

The Connectors catalog now groups connectors by what you want to build, such as Sell and get paid or Add AI to your apps. You can also search by describing what you want to do, such as sending invoices to customers.

Resize images and make videos in Files

You can now resize an image or turn it into a short video from the image editing toolbar in your project's Files tab. Resize changes the image's shape, such as to square or widescreen, and extends the scene to fill the new frame rather than cropping it. Make video animates the image. Select Add prompt and finish the prompt in the project chat, or select Quick animate. Lovable saves each result as a new file next to the original.

Removed: AI edits count in project settings

The AI edits count has been removed from your project's settings, because it counted activity rather than credits. Credit usage, in the same section, shows what the project has spent, with a link to its usage details.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 9, 2026
items.summary: App + chat connectors: Jira and Mailjet Jira lets apps search, create, and update issues on your Jira Cloud site and read its projects, boards, and sprints. Use it for sprint dashboards, bug and feedback intake forms, and triage views. Mailjet lets apps send…
items.html:
App + chat connectors: Jira and Mailjet

Jira lets apps search, create, and update issues on your Jira Cloud site and read its projects, boards, and sprints. Use it for sprint dashboards, bug and feedback intake forms, and triage views.

Mailjet lets apps send transactional email from a sender or domain you validated in Mailjet, add contacts to your contact lists, and read delivery status, such as sent, opened, clicked, or bounced. Use it for order confirmations, newsletter signups, and delivery dashboards.

Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Send your app's errors and performance data to Sentry

The Sentry connector now works in your app as well as in the project chat. Your app reports errors and performance data to your Sentry project with a client key (DSN). Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Connect to Resend with your own account

The Resend connector now lets you connect by signing in with your Resend account instead of pasting an API key. You authorize access for your Resend team, and Lovable refreshes that access automatically. Connecting with your own API key stays available.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 8, 2026
items.summary: Connect your app to PayPal You can now connect your Lovable app to PayPal to create checkouts, take the money after the buyer approves an order, issue refunds, and read order details in a PayPal account you already have. It fits shop checkouts, donation pages,…
items.html:
Connect your app to PayPal

You can now connect your Lovable app to PayPal to create checkouts, take the money after the buyer approves an order, issue refunds, and read order details in a PayPal account you already have. It fits shop checkouts, donation pages, ticket sales, and booking deposits. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 7, 2026
items.summary: Require approval to enable a backend in a project On Enterprise plans, a workspace policy can now require an admin or owner to approve before anyone enables Lovable backend services in a project. Lovable backend services is the built-in backend where an app's…
items.html:
Require approval to enable a backend in a project

On Enterprise plans, a workspace policy can now require an admin or owner to approve before anyone enables Lovable backend services in a project. Lovable backend services is the built-in backend where an app's database, user accounts, and file storage live. A member who asks Lovable for something that needs a backend sends a request with an optional message, and an admin or owner approves or denies it in the Action center. Admins and owners enable backend services without a request. Lovable sets the policy up for your workspace and enables it at the same time.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 6, 2026
items.summary: Approve requests to use your internally published app When someone outside the audience opens an app you published internally, they can now ask you for access, with an optional message. The request arrives in your Inbox, where you approve or decline it, and…
items.html:
Approve requests to use your internally published app

When someone outside the audience opens an app you published internally, they can now ask you for access, with an optional message. The request arrives in your Inbox, where you approve or decline it, and Lovable emails the person either way. When you approve, Lovable adds the person to the app's audience without publishing again. They get no access to the project. After a decline, they can ask again 24 hours later.

See why a connector request failed

Your project's Connectors view now has an Activity tab. It lists the requests your app and your project chat send through a connector, each with its status and how long it took, next to the success rate and median response time. On a failed request, select Fix with Lovable to put a message about it in the project chat, ready to send. You can also ask Lovable to check the records for you. Chat connectors, requests your app sends straight to a provider, and incoming webhooks are not recorded.

Connect your app to ActiveCampaign

You can now connect your Lovable app to ActiveCampaign to search contacts and update their details, create mailing lists and subscribe or unsubscribe contacts, schedule campaigns and read their performance, and build audience segments. It fits newsletter signup forms, contact directories, and campaign dashboards. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Chat connectors: Supermetrics

Supermetrics is now available as a prebuilt chat connector, so Lovable can browse your data sources, query metrics from your campaigns, analytics, and stores, and read your Supermetrics Studio dashboards while you build. You need a Supermetrics subscription that includes API access. Add it from Connectors.

GPT-6.1 Terra, GPT Image 2.6 Flare, and GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst for your app's AI features

Your app's AI features can now use three new OpenAI models:

  • GPT-6.1 Terra (openai/gpt-6.1-terra) for fast reasoning, image analysis, and writing at lower cost than GPT-6.1 Sol. It accepts text and image input and responds with text.
  • GPT Image 2.6 Flare (openai/gpt-image-2.6-flare), the faster of the two image models, for previews and in-app image editors.
  • GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst (openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst) for detailed visuals and precise edits.

Both image models can produce a short animated GIF, guide an edit with a drawing on the image, and produce a still image with a transparent background, as a PNG or WebP file. Generating and editing images uses credits, like other AI usage. None of the three models is available while EU inference is enabled.

Ask Lovable to use any of these models in your app, or describe what you want and let Lovable pick.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 5, 2026
items.summary: Report problems to Lovable from your MCP client You can now report a problem to Lovable from the AI client you connect to the Lovable MCP server. Ask the client to send a report when something gets in the way, such as a misread request, a stuck project, or a…
items.html:
Report problems to Lovable from your MCP client

You can now report a problem to Lovable from the AI client you connect to the Lovable MCP server. Ask the client to send a report when something gets in the way, such as a misread request, a stuck project, or a failed build. Sending a report is free.

App + chat connectors: Fortnox, Mailchimp, and Mailchimp Transactional

Fortnox lets apps read and manage the customers, suppliers, invoices, orders, articles, and bookkeeping in your Fortnox company. Use it for finance dashboards, invoicing workflows, and internal operations tools.

Mailchimp lets apps add and update contacts in an audience, tag them, read segments, and show campaign results such as opens, clicks, unsubscribes, and bounces. Use it for newsletter signups, contact management, and marketing dashboards.

Mailchimp Transactional lets apps send email from your verified sending domain, use your existing templates, schedule messages with attachments, and show recent delivery activity. Use it for order confirmations, appointment reminders, and receipts.

Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Topaz Starlight Fast 2 for your app's AI features

Your app's AI features can now use Topaz Starlight Fast 2 (topazlabs/starlight-fast-2). The model rebuilds the detail in a blurry, noisy, or low-resolution clip and returns it at 1080p or 4K, with the original frame rate. A restoration runs in the background and can take hours. Workspace admins and owners enable TopazLabs in Connectors → AI first. Ask Lovable to use the model in your app. Restoring a clip uses credits.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 4, 2026
items.summary: Dreaming: Lovable keeps its memory up to date Lovable now tidies up project memory in the background on paid plans, a process called Dreaming. Lovable checks its memory and the rules in your AGENTS.md files against your code and the project chat. Lovable then…
items.html:
Dreaming: Lovable keeps its memory up to date

Lovable now tidies up project memory in the background on paid plans, a process called Dreaming. Lovable checks its memory and the rules in your AGENTS.md files against your code and the project chat.

Lovable then rewrites or removes what no longer applies, and rules you asked for stay as written. Your app's code never changes, and AGENTS.md changes show in the project chat and in version history as Lovable tidied up its notes. Dreaming does not use credits.

Log in once when your SSO provider is Google

On Business and Enterprise plans, you now log in once when your workspace enforces SSO through Google. Select Continue with Google and use a Google Workspace account on your workspace's verified domain, and Lovable does not ask you to log in again.

See who you are publishing to

When you invite people outside your workspace to your published app, the audience list now shows each person's email address under their name. External invitees and collaborators are marked with an EXT label.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 3, 2026
items.summary: Lovable saves every form submission Ask Lovable for a form that visitors use to reach you, such as a contact, booking, or quote form, and Lovable now saves each submission to a table. Lovable tells you the table's name in the project chat. To get the…
items.html:
Lovable saves every form submission

Ask Lovable for a form that visitors use to reach you, such as a contact, booking, or quote form, and Lovable now saves each submission to a table. Lovable tells you the table's name in the project chat. To get the submissions by email as well, tell Lovable which address to send them to. Lovable sends those emails from a verified sender domain, which you set up on a paid plan.

Protect a project from abandonment cleanup

On Enterprise plans, you can now protect a project from cleanup so Lovable never marks it abandoned. A protected project is never deleted for inactivity. Enable Abandonment protection in your project's settings, or select Protect it on the abandoned project banner. Workspace admins and owners can protect any project in Security insights.

Lovable follows AGENTS.md files in your project's subfolders

Lovable now follows the AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files in your project's subfolders. When Lovable opens or edits a file, it reads the instruction files in that file's folder and in every folder above it.

Connect your app to Mollie

You can now connect your Lovable app to Mollie to create payments in your own Mollie account, send customers to Mollie's hosted checkout, and confirm each payment's status. It fits apps whose owners already take payments with Mollie through iDEAL, Bancontact, cards, and SEPA. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Redesigned Privacy & security settings

Your workspace's Privacy & security settings are now grouped in five tabs: Access, Publishing, Security, Integrations, and Data protection.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 2, 2026
items.summary: Project monitoring catches errors in your visitors' browsers On paid plans, project monitoring now also checks the errors that happen in your visitors' browsers. Lovable looks for the cause of those errors in your code and shows what it finds in the editor.…
items.html:
Project monitoring catches errors in your visitors' browsers

On paid plans, project monitoring now also checks the errors that happen in your visitors' browsers. Lovable looks for the cause of those errors in your code and shows what it finds in the editor. The project owner receives an email about important findings. Lovable collects browser errors only while Visitor analytics is enabled.

Choose whether Lovable personalizes its messages to you

You can now decide whether Lovable personalizes the messages it sends you. Find Use my activity to personalize communication in your account preferences. The setting is enabled by default, except in the EU, the rest of the European Economic Area, the UK, and Brazil.

Connect your app to BambooHR

You can now connect your Lovable app to BambooHR to look up and update employee records, read the company directory, and see who is out of office. It fits employee directories, out-of-office boards, and headcount dashboards. Add it from Connectors, or ask Lovable in a project to connect it.

Redesigned Action center reviews

The review dialogs in the Action center match Lovable's current design and now show each project's owner. A security review lists each open finding with its severity. In the same review, you can ignore every open finding at once. Select a project's name to open the project in a new tab.

Redesigned publishing and approval status

The Publish dialog now lists what stops you from publishing under Before you publish. Each item shows the action that resolves it. When your workspace requires approval, the dialog shows the status of your request, such as Awaiting review or Approved by with the approver's name.

Redesigned domain settings

Your project and workspace domain settings have a new layout. In a project, you buy a domain under Find and buy a domain. The page lists your connected domains with their status, such as Active or Needs attention. Your workspace settings list every domain in the workspace. Open a domain to see its alerts.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Nov 1, 2026
items.summary: Download an SBOM for your project You can now download a software bill of materials (SBOM) for your project from the dependency list in the Security view, in SPDX 2.3 or CycloneDX 1.5 format. The file lists your production dependencies and their known…
items.html:
Download an SBOM for your project

You can now download a software bill of materials (SBOM) for your project from the dependency list in the Security view, in SPDX 2.3 or CycloneDX 1.5 format. The file lists your production dependencies and their known vulnerabilities, so you can share it with a security or procurement team or load it into your own security tools. Downloading an SBOM is free.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 31, 2026
items.summary: Open a page of your app from Chats You can now ask Lovable in Chats to show you a page in one of your projects. Lovable opens the project's preview at that page, beside the conversation.
items.html:
Open a page of your app from Chats

You can now ask Lovable in Chats to show you a page in one of your projects. Lovable opens the project's preview at that page, beside the conversation.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 30, 2026
items.summary: Lovable remembers what you tell it Lovable now remembers the preferences, decisions, and facts you state as you build, and applies them in later conversations without being reminded. Project memory belongs to one project and is shared by everyone who can edit…
items.html:
Lovable remembers what you tell it

Lovable now remembers the preferences, decisions, and facts you state as you build, and applies them in later conversations without being reminded. Project memory belongs to one project and is shared by everyone who can edit it. Personal memory covers how you want Lovable to work with you, in every project you build.

Your workspace and project Memory settings show a plain-language summary of what Lovable remembers. To correct something, select the text and choose Change in chat. In the same settings, you choose which memory Lovable uses or disable it.

See progress and next steps when you publish

The Publish dialog now shows a progress bar while Lovable deploys your app. When your site is live, the dialog shows its address with options to visit and share it. The dialog also suggests next steps, such as getting more visitors or connecting a custom domain.

items.title: Lovable changelog — Oct 29, 2026
items.summary: Bring your app or website to Lovable You can now import a project that you built with another tool, or an existing website, and keep building it in Lovable. For a project from Replit, Bolt, Base44, v0, or Manus, export it as a ZIP and upload it. For a website,…
items.html:
Bring your app or website to Lovable

You can now import a project that you built with another tool, or an existing website, and keep building it in Lovable. For a project from Replit, Bolt, Base44, v0, or Manus, export it as a ZIP and upload it. For a website, including one built with Wix, Squarespace, or Webflow, enter its address. Start from Import project to Lovable in the + menu on your dashboard. Your first import is free. After that, imports are treated as standard build usage and consume credits.

Run a Deep scan from the project chat

You can now ask Lovable in the project chat to review your app's security, and Lovable starts a Deep scan in the background. Lovable also runs the Quick scan, and you can follow the Deep scan's progress in the Security view. When the Deep scan finishes, Lovable explains the findings in the chat. The scans are free. Your request and Lovable's explanation of the findings are treated as standard build usage and consume credits.

Move SSO to a new identity provider

Workspace admins and owners on Business and Enterprise plans can now move an SSO provider to a new identity provider without deleting it. Change the entity ID, issuer, or client ID on the provider's Connection tab. The provider keeps its settings, so Enforce SSO, SCIM, and the domain lock stay enabled.

Updated visit counting in Analytics and Insights

Analytics for your published apps now counts visits without storing anything on your visitors' devices, and filters out more bots. A reload or a new tab starts a new visit, so many apps show more visits from October 26, 2026. When the period you select starts before October 26 and includes it, the Analytics chart marks that day. Workspace Insights counts App visits the same way.

For periods that start on or after October 26, 2026, Engagement rate replaces Bounce rate. It shows the percentage of visits with at least two page views or at least 10 seconds of engagement.

Save files to Favorites

Each project's Files tab now has a Favorites collection for the files you want to find again. Select the bookmark icon on a file to add it. Everyone in the project sees the same favorites, and the collection cannot be renamed or deleted.

Log in with one click using Google

You can now log in to Lovable from Google's sign-in card. The card appears on the login and sign-up pages when your browser is signed in to Google. Select your account on the card, and Lovable logs you in, or creates an account if you don't have one. Two-factor authentication still applies.

Redesigned password page for preview links

The password page of a password-protected shared preview link that allows comments now matches Lovable's current design. Password-protected preview links are available on Business and Enterprise plans.
