items.html:
MOMO CODE v2.0.0 — Pi-based Converged Architecture

Major architecture upgrade. momo Code is an original work, not a fork of any project. The Pi framework is consumed as a third-party Apache-2.0 dependency. See NOTICE and LICENSE for details.

Highlights
  • Unified CLI entry (bin/momo) — one entry point for interactive REPL, Pi agent, and legacy /evolve /fine-tune modes
  • JEV decision layer — 5 decision points, shadow mode, ECE calibration
  • RSI 3-level self-evolution loop — R1/R2/R3 with budget control and AbortController
  • momo-bench — three-tier evaluation (selection / holdout / canary) + promotion gate with 7 reverse test cases
  • 6 Pi extensions — brand banner, CoT panel (⌃T), decision capsules, tactical experience injection, sensitive-operation Y/n confirmation, RSI signal collection
  • Interactive REPL — TTY entry with ⌃T / ⌃O / ⌃C keyboard bindings, collapsed/expanded CoT rendering, decision capsules with evidence bars
  • Experience closure — idempotent TaskExposure → TaskOutcome → Solidify loop
  • Contracts & types — DecisionPort (choice / bool / score / abstain), EvolutionCandidate + CAS guard, TaskResult + 8 event envelopes
  • Tests — e2e smoke (23 checks) + P0–P6 integration tests
Changed
  • Simulated Math.random() paths explicitly marked with [SIMULATED] warnings
  • Added @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.1.0 and tsx; new smoke / loop / bench scripts

Full changelog: see CHANGELOG.md and the v2.0.0 project structure in README.md.

items.title: Cleanyourtv App v0.4.8 — Clean Your TV
items.summary: Clean Your TV app 0.4.8 fixes the new home screen's install on Google TVs, brings the new home screen to four more TVs, and makes Check for updates work again. Thank you to everyone who tested the 0.4.8 test builds, sent reports and told us what happened after…
items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.8 fixes the new home screen's install on Google TVs, brings the new home screen to four more TVs, and makes Check for updates work again.

Thank you to everyone who tested the 0.4.8 test builds, sent reports and told us what happened after a restart. Your answers decided which TVs get the new home screen in this release, and you're on our testers page. To see what the app does on your TV, search the TV list.

What's new

The new home screen installs again on Google TVs. On Google TVs with Android 11 and 12 (Sony BRAVIA, TCL, Xiaomi, Hisense, the TiVo Stream 4K and others), the switch could stop at "Install com.gathin.tvhome" with "got no readable apk", run after run. The new home screen was on the TV but not installed for the TV's main user. The app now installs it for that user (#2743, #1918, #1510 and many more). If the check still can't read the app, the report says why.

The new home screen on four more TVs, with the setup wizard left on:

  • the Xiaomi MiTV-MOEU1 on Android 14
  • the MI MiProjM05 projector on Android 9
  • the Strong LEAP-S1 box on Android 14
  • the Toshiba Smart TV (hamamatsucho) on Android 11

Each one was confirmed by two testers whose new home screen was still there after a restart, and nobody said it didn't hold. Only these models: other models of these brands keep their own home screen until their own testers confirm it.

Clearer stops.

  • When the TV ends the install part way ("the TV closed the stream"), the app reads the TV's free storage and says when there isn't enough space (#2851, #3221).
  • When Android shows its "which home screen?" chooser, the card names the other home screen apps on the TV, so you know which to remove (#3301).
  • On Google TVs other than TCL, the app says before the switch that the remote's Settings button may stop opening the TV's own settings panel (#3059). Use the TV's own home screen in Manage brings it back.

Connecting. Enter the TV's address on the waiting screen works. When the TV turns the connection away, the card says debugging is off on the TV instead of blaming the phone. Manage finds a TV again that it last saw with debugging off.

Smaller fixes: "Check for updates" works again (#818, #2486); Undo everything plans from a fresh read of the TV (#2825); Live TV gets a dock tile on more TVs (#1902); Manage's dock list offers the apps the TV can open, Play Store included (#2742); a failed install no longer also reports "look not sent".

The Home button helper from the test builds isn't in this release yet. It stays in the test builds while we finish it.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.4.8.apk below and open it on your phone (Android 9 or newer, on the same Wi-Fi as the TV). It installs over 0.4.7 and the 0.4.8 test builds and keeps everything. On 0.4.7 or older, Check for updates can't find this version by itself (that was the bug fixed here), so download it from this page. If your TV kept its own home screen before, open it in the app and tap Run Setup again.

If anything goes wrong, tap Report a problem in the app. Undo everything in Manage puts the TV back the way it was.

Verify

  • Signer certificate SHA-256: eaf7af3867bb29ff4bb038854842c93f42ffe4198a087e611cb18f925201cd65 (the same key as every release)

items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.7 brings the new home screen to more TVs, and everything from the 0.4.7 test builds.

Thank you to everyone who tested the 0.4.6 and 0.4.7 test builds, restarted their TV and told us what happened. Your answers decided which TVs get the new home screen in this release, and you're on our testers page. To see what the app does on your TV, search the TV list.

What's new

The new home screen on more TVs, with the setup wizard left on. On TVs with Google's Android TV home screen, the new home screen takes over while the TV's setup wizard stays on, so your Wi-Fi isn't touched. 0.4.6 did this for Xiaomi and Redmi on Android 9 to 11. 0.4.7 adds:

  • OnePlus TVs on Android 11
  • Sony TVs on Android 8
  • Hisense TVs on Android 9
  • Homatics boxes on Android 14
  • MECOOL boxes on Android 14
  • the Xiaomi MiTV-MZTU1 on Android 14
  • "My" Android TV sets (yeoksam, shandao and tokyo) on Android 11

Each one was confirmed by at least two testers whose new home screen was still there after a restart, and nobody said it didn't hold. The safety checks stay: a TV whose setup wizard or another app answers the Home button keeps its own home screen. More brands come as testers confirm them.

The look and wallpaper reach more TVs. On some TVs (Xiaomi and TCL with Android 11, Android 14 boxes) Android refused the app's copy of the look. The app now hands the look to the home screen itself.

Clearer screens. When the TV keeps its own home screen, every screen says so first, with the reason, and doesn't offer looks that can't apply.

The app counts restarts. After a switch, each time the app connects it checks whether the TV restarted and whether the new home screen is still answering Home. When a restart held, Tell us it worked opens a short, prefilled confirmation for GitHub (no names, addresses or serial numbers, and nothing is sent until you post it).

This is your TV now. After a look goes to the TV, the app shows the TV's own screenshot, with "Not right? Send it again".

Manage reconnects by itself after the TV restarts or you come back to the app, and no longer waits forever when your phone is on a different Wi-Fi than at setup. The waiting screen says what's wrong, and Connection details makes a short text to share with us (no full addresses, Wi-Fi names or serial numbers).

Safety fixes from your reports:

  • Xiaomi MiTV-MOOQ0: the factory test app now really goes off before the TV's own home screen, so Home can't land on a factory test screen (#1944).
  • Skyworth SWTV-22AE-FHD: My Apps and the daily manager stay on, which the remote's custom button needs (#1378).
  • Boxes with an operator's own home screen ranked above ours (Jio's on the JMSB200A, #2028) keep their home screen.
  • The MOKA board sold under Panasonic and other brands gets no home screen switch, like the rest of that family.

Smaller fixes: "Check for updates" works on more networks; the dock has a Live TV row on more TVs and no empty spaces; reports show the app's version again; Customise names your own photo look.

The Home button helper from the test builds isn't in this release yet. It stays in the test builds while we finish it.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.4.7.apk below and open it on your phone (Android 9 or newer, on the same Wi-Fi as the TV). It installs over 0.4.6.1 and the 0.4.7 test builds and keeps everything. If your TV is in the list above and kept its own home screen before, open it in the app and tap Run Setup again.

If anything goes wrong, tap Report a problem in the app. Undo everything in Manage puts the TV back the way it was.

items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.6.1 fixes one thing: reconnecting to a TV that got a new Wi-Fi address.

The problem

After a TV software update, or on a mesh Wi-Fi, a TV can get a new address. The app only tried the address it saved the first time, so Manage stayed "Offline" and waited for the TV forever, even with debugging switched on.

The fix

When the saved address doesn't answer, the app looks for the same TV on your Wi-Fi, the way "Add a TV" does, and saves its new address. It checks it's really your TV first (the TV must recognise this phone and have the same ID), so it never connects to another TV, and a TV that already trusted your phone doesn't ask you to allow it again.

Nothing else changes from 0.4.6.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.4.6.1.apk below and open it on your phone (Android 9 or newer, on the same Wi-Fi as the TV). It installs over 0.4.6 and keeps everything. If you're on the 0.4.7-beta1 test build, you already have this fix.

items.summary: Clean Your TV app 0.4.6 gives Xiaomi and Redmi TVs on Google's Android TV home the new home screen, adds a one-tap "Report a problem" button, and makes the home screen switch safer, with fixes that came straight from testers' reports. What's new The new home…
items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.6 gives Xiaomi and Redmi TVs on Google's Android TV home the new home screen, adds a one-tap "Report a problem" button, and makes the home screen switch safer, with fixes that came straight from testers' reports.

What's new

  • The new home screen on Xiaomi and Redmi TVs on Android 9, 10 and 11 that have no list of their own, such as the Mi TV 4i. Their setup wizard stays on and your Wi-Fi isn't touched. A Xiaomi TV with a home screen app you installed yourself gets it too, and your app stays installed.
  • Report a problem on every stop, timeout, paused change and connect problem. One tap opens a ready-filled GitHub issue in your browser, so there's nothing to paste. The app itself still sends nothing: nothing is public until you post it.
  • Run Setup again. If an earlier version left your home screen alone, for example before your TV had a list of its own, Manage now says so and offers to run Setup again.
  • Honest reasons. When another home screen app or a vendor service is why the app left the home screen alone, Setup and Manage say exactly that.

Safer home screen switch

  • TVs where a vendor service also answers the Home button keep their own home screen. One such TV failed to start after its home screen was switched in a test build.
  • On Xiaomi TVs, Mi TV+ and PatchWall's web content stay on while PatchWall stays on, because PatchWall can open at start-up. If an earlier version switched them off, Setup switches them back on before it changes the home screen.
  • Each time you open Manage, the app checks the Home button again and tells you if the TV's setup wizard could take it.
  • Right after the switch, if the TV brings up Live TV in front of the new home screen, the app presses Home again for you.

Fixes

  • Manage, the Restore point page and Done all show the restore point that "Undo everything" goes back to.
  • Manage no longer stays on "Working" after "Stop and undo".
  • Reports fold repeated connection retries into one line, so more of what happened fits.
  • The home screen switch no longer stops before it starts when the TV's screenshot is large (a 4K screen, or a detailed wallpaper). A safety check refused screenshots over 2 MB, nothing was changed, and the old home screen came back after a restart. Reports now also say which check stopped a switch, and why the TV refused a step.

Known issue

  • On some TVs (seen on Xiaomi and TCL with Android 11, and Android 14 boxes) Android doesn't let the app copy the look and wallpaper into the new home screen. The new home screen works with its default look, nothing else changes, and the fix comes in 0.4.7.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.4.6.apk below and open it on an Android 9 or newer phone with a screen lock, on the same Wi-Fi as your Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV. It installs over any earlier version, including the 0.4.6 test builds, and keeps everything. If the app opens Manage for your TV, tap Run Setup again to use what's new.

Verify

  • Signer certificate SHA-256: eaf7af3867bb29ff4bb038854842c93f42ffe4198a087e611cb18f925201cd65 (apksigner verify --print-certs cleanyourtv-0.4.6.apk)
  • Reproducible: the unsigned build is 5d877ced402f48795b55e7e04e8f5d518c998db50e096d4bf2a654f37e1e27ac, the same from two clean builds; scripts/verify-release.sh checks that this APK is that build plus a signature.
  • Commit 6dbb574a, upstream Clean Your TV b06ab21 (home screen 3.0).

Credits

A community-built phone app for Clean Your TV by Gathin, used with his permission. The home screen and the TV lists come from Clean Your TV and its community. Thank you to the 53 people who tested the app on their own TVs this week: every fix above started with one of your reports.

items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.5 brings the 3.0 home screen from Gathin's Clean Your TV, more choices in the Look sheet, 25 more TV lists (173 in all), and fixes for phones on Android 9 to 12 that could not connect to a new TV.

What's new

  • Home screen 3.0. A TV that has the home screen from an earlier version sees "Update the home screen" in Manage. Nothing changes until you tap it, and the update keeps your look, your dock and your remote buttons.
  • More Look options on home screen 3.0: every app in one row, a dock with no band, the greeting on or off, the date under the clock, a brighter date, a warning colour on the Wi-Fi icon when the internet is down, app tiles as icons on cards, and a rim or halo highlight. The preview shows each one before anything reaches the TV, and looks you already sent stay exactly as they are.
  • 25 more TV lists from Clean Your TV, among them NVIDIA SHIELD TV (2017), Philips Google TV TA1 and TA7, Sony BRAVIA VU1 and VU3, TCL G08 (EU, Android 12), OnePlus TV (Cebu and Dosa), Xiaomi Mi Box S (Android 12) and several Xiaomi Mi TVs. The Sony BRAVIA BF1 list now matches BF1 sets, and lists we already had got their contributors' fixes.
  • Better back on. If this app switched off something a TV's list now keeps on, like a TCL remote's mic service, Manage says so and offers to switch it back on.
  • PatchWall on Xiaomi TVs is now your choice, so the remote's PatchWall button keeps working.

Fixes

  • Phones on Android 9 to 12 can connect to a new TV again. The TV never showed Allow and the app said "unreachable". Saving a restore file on phones below Android 15 is fixed too.
  • Some TCL Smart TV Pro sets on Google TV got a list made for the Android TV version, so the app left their home screen alone. They now get the right set.
  • Connection errors say what went wrong instead of "unreachable". A TV that leaves the Wi-Fi mid-run pauses the run instead of hanging.
  • "Try again" after a home screen check that timed out now really tries again, and the last screen says honestly when the home screen stayed.
  • Safer undo: "Undo everything" is no longer refused for protected apps, never switches accessibility on, and never treats a chooser screen as your home screen.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Install

Download cleanyourtv-0.4.5.apk below and open it on an Android 9 or newer phone with a screen lock, on the same Wi-Fi as your Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV. It installs over any earlier version and keeps everything.

items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.4.0 brings a new Look sheet for your TV's home screen: pick a picture, one of five styles and how many apps sit in a row, and see your own TV in a preview before anything reaches it.

What's new

  • Five styles, each shown as a small preview of your TV with your picture: Classic (a dark dock, a big name and a soft glow), Glass (a frosted dock and light in each app's colour), Spotlight (a big banner of the app you are on, with the app's colour across the top), All apps (every app in one grid) and Calm (no glow and no big name, just apps and your picture).
  • Pictures for any style: Mist, Aurora, Navy, Autumn lake, Curtains, Mountains (with a sky that changes with the hour), Lamp light, Neon, Cobalt, no picture, or your own photo, cropped on the phone. Diwali is there until 10 November, with its lamps and festive icons. The pictures are our own work, free to use (CC0).
  • 4 to 8 apps in a row. Fewer apps means bigger tiles. "Names under every app" puts each app's name under its tile, easier to read from the sofa.
  • More options: how the highlight moves (Lively, Smooth, Quick or Off), the big name, the glow, a ring in the app's colour, the dock band (solid, see-through or glass), the buttons at the top and a green Wi-Fi icon. Advanced has lift and zoom, see-through amount, sky strength and the settings file itself.
  • Nothing is sent until you tap "Put it on the TV". "Undo changes" takes the sheet back to how it opened, and "Put back the earlier look" brings back the look the TV had before your last send.
  • Your dock keeps its order when you go to fewer apps in a row, and empty spaces stay empty on the TV.
  • Setup's Look step is the same sheet, with Done at the bottom.
  • A look you picked before this version stays on the TV exactly as it is until you send a new one.
  • TCL: picking TCL under "Change model" now asks whether the TV's menus are in English (or your language) or in Chinese, so TCL TVs sold outside China get the right steps to connect.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Install

  • Updated lists. Ten lists changed upstream and follow it, among them the Hisense SmartTV 4K FFM, the Sony BRAVIA 4K UR2 and VH2, the TCL G05 and G09 Google TV and the Xiaomi TV A Pro 2026. The Xiaomi MiTV-AESP0 list keeps its setup wizard on, as in 0.3.6. Hisense TVs without an exact list also switch off Google partner setup and Calendar sync.

  • The home screen app 2.7. With its default settings the TV looks as before, with fixes: the network pill shows the VPN badge right away, the dock's corners follow its tiles, Launcher settings changes apply when you leave with Home, and the quick settings no longer crash on Android 8.0. It also speaks Ukrainian. Its new options are all off by default; the app lets you choose them in a later version. A TV set up with an earlier version is offered "Update the home screen" in Manage.

By any list, also during the home screen switch: vendor setup wizards (OnePlus, Xiaomi and Android's device provisioning), vendor home screens (Haier, OnePlus), TalkBack and Google's text-to-speech, the Sony accessibility tutorial and the TCL hearing aid, the remote's services (the Google TV remote service and its logger, Sony remote start and the OnePlus remote diagnosis), the Xiaomi TV service and TCL Live. items.summary: Clean Your TV app 0.3.6 fixes TVs that got stuck after a home screen switch rolled back and the install that kept saying the TV stopped answering. Thank you to everyone who sent a report and a log: each of these fixes starts from one. What's new No more stuck…
items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.6 fixes TVs that got stuck after a home screen switch rolled back and the install that kept saying the TV stopped answering. Thank you to everyone who sent a report and a log: each of these fixes starts from one.

What's new

  • No more stuck Setup after a rollback. When the home screen switch rolled back, Setup offered "Try with the wizard off", which saved a choice that every later plan refused, and Back led to Welcome instead of the TV's restore options. That card is gone, saved choices the TV would refuse are dropped before planning, and Back on a refused plan opens Manage for a TV this app already changed (#375, #385).
  • No more endless "TV stopped answering" during an install. Some TVs end the app's install with an error while staying connected. The app now checks whether the install landed: done if it did, otherwise that step fails and Setup carries on with the clean-up, without the home screen switch (#80, #364, #367).
  • A heads-up on TCL Google TV. Before the switch, the plan screen and Manage > Home screen say that the remote's Settings (gear), Netflix and YouTube buttons don't work with the new home screen, and that Use the TV's own home screen brings them back (#275).
  • A stricter safety rule for the setup wizard. The home screen switch is never planned while the TV shows a setup wizard that can take the Home button and the switch would leave it on, also on TVs with an exact list such as the Sony BRAVIA BF1. Those TVs get the clean-up alone. The TCL G10 Google TV list switches the wizard off as part of the switch, so it keeps its switch.
  • Reports list what was switched off. The problem report now has "Switched off by this app", so a reply can say exactly what to put back.
  • Better logs, and Copy error. The diagnostics log now says why a connection failed, what the TV showed when the home check rolled back, and the step the switch stopped at. When the TV answers but the phone can't connect, the door says what on the phone can block the app (a per-app network limit on MIUI or Samsung, a VPN, Private DNS, mobile data) and offers Copy error: a short summary with no addresses in it, ready to paste into an issue.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

Clean Your TV app 0.3.5 gives more TVs a careful clean-up and adds a safety guard for the ACER R4G. Thank you to everyone who sent a TV report: the list of apps in each one showed us what is safe to switch off on TVs nobody has tested yet.

What's new

  • More TVs get a careful clean-up. TVs from brands with one or two tested lists (Skyworth, SHARP, onn, OnePlus, Haier and others) now switch off up to six hidden feedback and advertising services: Google Feedback and its consent prompt, the print service, and Android's on-device advertising, ad personalization and ad model services. Before, these TVs got no clean-up unless a list matched the exact model (#89, #108, #169, #194, #196, #251).
  • Nothing else changes on those TVs. The home screen decision is the same as before, and the app still checks each switch-off on the TV before it runs it. TVs that already had a brand set get nothing new.
  • A safety guard for the ACER R4G. It is made by MOKA, in the same family as the TVs whose setup wizard comes back at every restart, so Setup never offers the home screen switch on it and does the clean-up alone (#74, #102).
  • Reports say which set was used. A TV report from one of these TVs now says Profile: brand set <Brand> instead of none.

items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.4 fixes "plan refused" on TVs whose home screen was already changed by another tool, and makes Setup honest when it can't make a safe plan. Thank you to everyone who sent a report with the log: it showed us exactly where it went wrong.

What's new

  • A home screen installed another way is left as it is. Some TVs already had the new home screen from the Clean Your TV tool for computers, which signs it with a different key. Setup used to stop with "plan refused" on every try. Now it leaves that home screen as it is and does the clean-up (#171, #187, #220).
  • An honest message when there is no safe plan. Setup used to say "We couldn't read what's on the TV" even though the TV had answered. Now it says it couldn't make a plan it is sure is safe, that nothing was changed, and Report a problem sends us the reason (#82, #99, #45).
  • Manage explains it too. On those TVs, Home screen says Setup left the home screen as it was, instead of offering a dock and a look for it.
  • Reports name the reason. The diagnostics log now says why a plan was refused. Apps you installed yourself are never named.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.3 fixes the issues people reported on the app's first public day. Thank you all: every report made this release better.

What's new

  • A TV that keeps something on no longer stops Setup. Some TVs answer "yes" when the app switches an app off, then keep it on. Setup now skips it, runs the rest of the clean-up, and Done names what wouldn't switch off. Before, Carry on met the same step again every time (#10).
  • Your own launcher is safe. A launcher you installed yourself is never switched off. If the TV's home screen was already changed, by another app or an earlier change, Setup leaves it as it is and does the clean-up, instead of "plan refused" (#8).
  • Honest Done screens. When nothing was changed, Done says so, and why (#15).
  • Manage explains the home screen. On a TV that kept its own home screen, Manage says why and what would change it, instead of a dock and a look that ended in "We stopped" (#3).
  • Reports fill the form in for you. Help add this TV and Report a problem now put the report straight into the GitHub form, and the report box can't be posted empty (#12, #14, #16).
  • Build numbers like "V816.0.11.0" are no longer masked as network addresses in reports.

items.html:
Clean Your TV app 0.3.2 fixes the first issues people reported, and makes it easy to report a problem or a TV the app doesn't know yet. Thank you to everyone who took the time to write in.

What's new

  • Fire TV sets are recognised on their own. Fire TV and Fire TV Edition TVs (Insignia, Toshiba and others) are now recognised from the TV's own details, even when the app has no list for the exact model. They get the clean-up only: Fire OS doesn't let another home screen take over, so the app no longer tries (#2).
  • Undo can't get stuck any more. Undo now checks the TV itself: if the TV's own home screen is back, undo is done, even when the TV refuses a step that is already in place. If 0.3.1 left you on "The setup didn't finish", it clears the next time the app connects to the TV after updating.
  • A way out, always. Stop here shows Done only once the run has really stopped, and "Forget this TV" ends an unfinished setup for that TV.
  • Help add this TV. When the app doesn't know your TV yet, one tap makes a short report of what the TV is and which apps it came with. Apps you installed yourself are only counted, never named. You read the whole text first, then paste it into a pre-filled GitHub form or share it another way. The app sends nothing itself (#1).
  • Report a problem, in Settings and on the screens where something went wrong, does the same with the app's log. The log is now readable: plain error names, how the TV was matched, and the step that failed with the TV's answer.
  • Privacy: the policy now describes these reports and the app's own log, which "Delete everything" also clears. Nothing new is collected.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

items.summary: The first public release of Clean Your TV app, a community-built phone app for Clean Your TV. Anyone can now clean up an Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV from an Android phone: no laptop, no coding agent, no cables. The app switches off adverts, tracking and…
items.html:
The first public release of Clean Your TV app, a community-built phone app for Clean Your TV. Anyone can now clean up an Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV from an Android phone: no laptop, no coding agent, no cables. The app switches off adverts, tracking and preloaded apps, installs the calm Clean Your TV home screen with a dock of the apps you use, shows its progress on the TV, and keeps a restore point so every change can be put back.

Highlights

  • 131 community tested TV profiles from 46 brands, plus a careful brand fallback for models nobody has profiled yet.
  • Launcher 2.5 (upstream v2.5.0): edit the dock from the remote, rows and wallpaper in Launcher settings, and more. A dock changed on the TV survives a new look from the phone.
  • A plan first. See what will be switched off and what is kept; Customise shows every command in order before it runs.
  • Restore point and undo, one app or everything, plus a restore copy with plain scripts that work from any computer with adb.
  • A watchdog on the TV puts its own home screen back if the phone does not confirm the new one within 150 seconds.
  • Stricter safety: the app never switches off what drives the HDMI and tuner inputs, accessibility or the remote, and on TVs where switching the home screen is known to cause trouble (Chromecast with Google TV, the Google TV Streamer, some Kalley and PRISM+ sets, TVs whose setup wizard must stay on) it does the clean-up only and says why.
  • No accounts, no analytics; internet only to GitHub, and only when you ask.

Full list of changes: CHANGELOG.md.

items.summary: FuXi 0.1.8 Release Announcement Release Date: September 22, 2026 We are pleased to announce the release of FuXi 0.1.8, a major update following 0.1.7. This release introduces rate-limit banners and an official plugin marketplace mirror, and delivers systematic…
items.html:
FuXi 0.1.8 Release Announcement

Release Date: September 22, 2026

We are pleased to announce the release of FuXi 0.1.8, a major update following 0.1.7. This release introduces rate-limit banners and an official plugin marketplace mirror, and delivers systematic stabilization and refinement across session storage, the engine, permissions, Windows compatibility, and the user interface.

New Features

  • Rate-limit banners: unified rate-limit data now feeds subscription banners; usage beyond the limit is silently rolled into additional usage with clear notification.
  • Official plugin marketplace mirror: the plugin marketplace is now served from an official GCS mirror, making plugin installs more stable and reliable.

Performance

  • Smoother long-session interactions: estimated scroll offsets and zero render-time filesystem syscalls reduce a cold first frame from ~1.6s (1000 lines) to ~160ms; scrolling performance is now independent of line count.
  • Faster resume & reads: a resume reads the transcript only once (34MB: 4.6s → 0.8s); sessions larger than 5MiB are read through a precompacted fast path in 1MB sequential chunks (~4.9× on a 30MB transcript); write-side 100ms batching keeps the disk format unchanged.
  • Streaming render fix: the linkify O(n²) full-render issue is resolved (20KB single line: 278ms → 2.9ms); streaming output no longer appears non-streaming.

Sessions & Messages

  • Session storage-chain optimization: a precompact read fast path, write-side batching, and live-cache re-append are introduced (metadata such as titles and tags flush synchronously, and external SDK writes are absorbed via a 64KB tail window).
  • Message-chain integrity: parentUuid chains now fully link every participant, with automatic re-linking after forks; switching sessions no longer loses in-flight messages; a unified session UUID registry fixes the /clear cache invalidation issue.

Permissions & Security

  • Dialog & rules: the permission dialog now uses a numbered Select list; "Always Allow" clearly displays the exact rule to be persisted; low-risk file commands (mkdir/cp/mv/touch/rmdir) are relaxed to command-name prefix rules.
  • Stability & Bash safety: the whole-UI freeze caused by permission dialogs is resolved (approval sends are now non-blocking); the Bash read-only gate is hardened (backticks and newlines can no longer bypass auto-approval); permission suggestions are built once per request and differentiated by reason.

Windows Compatibility

  • Startup & rendering: when Git for Windows is missing, startup now provides installation guidance directly (no longer stuck behind the login flow); CJK console glyphs and borders adapt to terminal capabilities, resolving mojibake, tofu, and input-box jitter; subprocess output is decoded strictly as UTF-8.

Engine & Tools

  • Non-streaming fallback: on empty or interrupted streams, the current turn is automatically retried via a non-streaming request.
  • Tool-execution dedup: a tool state machine and tracker form a dedup closed loop, eliminating duplicate tool cards.
  • Tool behavior unification: Read, Write, Edit, Notebook, and PDF tools now share consistent behavior and error messages; non-standard error prefixes are removed.

UI / MCP / Misc

  • UI: the task list is deduplicated (the right sidebar is the single task surface); the plan-approval dialog fits exactly, with buttons remaining visible on long plans.
  • MCP: the command allowlist is re-seeded after configuration reloads (servers added at runtime are no longer blocked); ~/.fuxi.json global configuration is unified.

Installation & Upgrade

Installation scripts automatically fetch the latest version with integrity verification.

macOS / Linux

curl -fsSL https://downloads.fuxicode.com/bootstrap.sh | bash

Windows (PowerShell)

irm https://downloads.fuxicode.com/bootstrap.ps1 | iex

Windows (CMD)

curl -fsSL https://downloads.fuxicode.com/install.cmd -o %TEMP%\install.cmd && %TEMP%\install.cmd

Existing users can upgrade by re-running the corresponding command. For issues, please report them at https://github.com/fuxicodex/Fuxi/issues.

FuXi 0.1.6 Release Announcement

Release Date: September 7, 2026

FuXi 0.1.6 is now available. This release focuses on core experience consistency and stability: unified session and message handling, hardened login flow, cross-platform compatibility improvements, and a number of stability fixes.

New Features

  • Unified session & message handling: chat messages are consolidated into a single message model, removing inconsistencies between multiple handling paths; message parent-child chains are preserved more completely, and partially-compacted history survives session resume.
  • Hardened login flow: cross-process token refresh is serialized to prevent token-chain failure; tokens are refreshed proactively before expiry to avoid forced re-login; login no longer times out — it waits until the user cancels.
  • Model selection validation: the /model command now validates that the selected model is supported by the current endpoint, giving clear feedback when an invalid model name is entered.

Improvements & Fixes

  • Engine: empty responses automatically retry via non-streaming requests; fixed repeated injection of external file changes and conditional memory; coordinator queue drained before every request; gateway length errors correctly recognized as context-window overflows.
  • Bash / Windows: unified command-line parsing reduces misclassification; strict UTF-8 subprocess output on Windows avoids garbled text; nested-heredoc crash fixed; startup git-bash check and working-directory exclusion added.
  • UI & Rendering: markdown rendering improvements, box-drawing table format, sidebar reasoning state and session cost, and chat lag fixed on huge content; CJK character-width handling now applies only to legacy Windows consoles.
  • Tasks / Agent: standardized task IDs and output paths; notification queue priorities (immediate / later / next); stricter stop-task conditions; agent_busy claim check.
  • Files & Search: more accurate search timeouts; staged protection for very large file reads; Grep content checks and UNC path handling fixed.
  • MCP: /mcp toggle persisted per-project; improved port allocation and lock-backoff; staged truncation for tool output.
  • Permission & Sandbox: static directory rules support subtree matching; sandbox configuration now takes effect with settings; unified session grant logic.
  • Context compaction: staged decision for file restore after compaction; improved shared-cache partial compaction.
  • Image recognition: recognition configuration is endpoint-scoped and no longer affects the main model's vision judgment; recognition-model refusals are never cached.

Installation / Upgrade

Installation scripts fetch the latest version automatically with integrity verification.

Windows (PowerShell)

irm https://fuxicode.com/install.ps1 | iex

Windows (CMD)

curl -fsSL https://fuxicode.com/install.cmd -o %TEMP%\install.cmd && %TEMP%\install.cmd

macOS (x64 / ARM64)

curl -fsSL https://fuxicode.com/install.sh | bash

Linux (x64 / ARM64)

Existing users can upgrade by re-running the corresponding command. For issues, please report them at https://github.com/fuxicodex/Fuxi/issues.

FuXi 0.1.2 Release Announcement

Release Date: August 6, 2026

FuXi 0.1.2 is now available, with major improvements across multi-window coordination, image capabilities, and the plugin ecosystem.

New Features

  • Multi-window coordination: switch seamlessly between concurrent sessions without interrupting your current work.
  • Image captioning: non-vision models can now generate image descriptions automatically, enabled by default.
  • Vision capability is automatically detected from known provider capabilities, with no manual configuration required.

Improvements & Fixes

  • Unified MCP plugin lifecycle: plugins from manifest, channel declarations, session plugins, and other sources all load under one consistent contract.
  • Multiple security hardening improvements: plaintext MCP tokens removed, OAuth credentials scoped to their trust domains, plugin secrets kept out of prompts, and plugin reloads no longer expose stale state.
  • Path traversal is blocked before normalization, preventing path escape risks.
  • Memory extraction now runs asynchronously, with an optimized memory_saved card.
  • Model cache isolation stays stable across sessions, and compacted context remains consistent across TUI turns.
  • Each model gets a stable user identity, and long prompts are preserved intact across the OpenAPI boundary.
  • Plugin LSP lifecycle options are supported, and usable LSP plugins are recommended after real file edits.

items.html:
Tiny Engineer v0.2.0

v0.2.0 is a big step toward making Tiny Engineer something you can actually build, customize, and keep improving — not just a cool prototype.

Since v0.1.0, 66 commits landed across hardware, CAD, firmware, integrations, and documentation.

From prototype to buildable project

The biggest change is the new parametric CAD model. Tiny Engineer now supports both FS0307 and SG90 servos, automated STL/STEP/3MF exports, parametric mounts and covers, tolerance tests, and multiple mechanical fixes.

There is also a proper mechanical assembly guide, measured screw list, improved shopping lists, and models prepared for external 3D printing.

From wires to a real board

Tiny Engineer is also moving toward much cleaner electronics.

This release introduces:

  • new integrated PCB combining USB-C, servo control, audio, power distribution and peripheral connections
  • KiCad tooling and manufacturing checks for JLCPCB

It replaces a pile of modules and wires with one reproducible board, while the advanced path using individual modules remains fully supported.

From developer setup to “plug it in”

Getting firmware onto the robot is now dramatically easier.

Tiny Engineer now has a browser-based Web Flasher, versioned firmware builds, downloadable CI artifacts and OTA firmware + filesystem updates.

First-time setup also gained a configuration wizard, servo calibration, better servo testing and configurable hostname.

More agents. More personality.

Tiny Engineer can now react to Claude Code and Antigravity CLI, alongside Cursor.

The robot itself also got more expressive: kaomoji, new cover and dots eye styles, improved sleep/wake animations, a dead state with sound, safer servo idle behavior and diagnostic RGB blink codes.

And there is now an official mods workflow — starting with the Halloween pumpkin-head variant. 🎃

❤️ Community

A significant part of this release came from community contributions.

Special thanks to:

  • @jtruland — Claude Code integration, ESP32 carrier board, diagnostics and setup improvements
  • @Mechazawa — OTA firmware and filesystem updates
  • @Hilo-Hilo — parametric bottom cover and chair mounts
  • @AndreLYL — kaomoji expression system
  • @rarephill — Antigravity CLI integration

And thank you to everyone else who contributed code, fixes, documentation, ideas, testing, and feedback since v0.1.0.

Tiny Engineer is becoming a much better project because people are building it together.

Full changelog

Hardware & CAD
  • Parametric FS0307 + SG90 model
  • STL, STEP and 3MF export workflow
  • Parametric bottom cover and chair mounts
  • Screw/servo tolerance test models
  • Compact ESP32-C3 carrier board
  • Main Control Board
  • Integrated production-oriented PCB
  • KiCad/JLCPCB tooling and validation
  • Multiple servo, neck, bell, lamp, keyboard and mounting fixes
  • External 3D-printing preparation
Firmware & UX
  • Web-based firmware flashing
  • OTA firmware + filesystem updates
  • Versioned builds and firmware artifacts
  • First-time setup wizard + servo calibration
  • Configurable hostname
  • Servo PWM shutdown when idle
  • Subsystem diagnostic blink codes
  • Improved boot, sleep and wake behavior
Personality & integrations
  • Claude Code integration
  • Antigravity CLI integration
  • Improved Cursor hooks
  • MacBook sleep/wake integration
  • Kaomoji expressions
  • cover and dots OLED eye styles
  • Improved sleep animations
  • Dead-state animation + audio
Project
  • Mechanical assembly guide
  • Updated screw/BOM/shopping documentation
  • CI firmware compile/package tests
  • Contribution and PR templates
  • Coding-agent guidelines
  • Mods workflow + Halloween example
  • General README, CAD, assets and integration documentation improvements

Flash offsets (default USB layout)

File Offset
tiny-engineer-v0.2.0-bootloader.bin 0x0
tiny-engineer-v0.2.0-partitions.bin 0x8000
tiny-engineer-v0.2.0-firmware.bin 0x10000
tiny-engineer-v0.2.0-littlefs.bin 0x220000

All four files are required for a clean first flash or web install. App + LittleFS alone is enough only when bootloader and partition table are already on the chip.

Web flash: jamro.github.io/tiny-engineer/flash/ — pick this tag (or any release that ships manifest.json). Offsets above match this tag’s partitions.csv. Usual path: clone the tagged commit and run pio run -t upload (see docs/flash.md).

items.html:
DeepCode v2.3.1 is a stability release for the terminal UI on the shared background service. Answers now appear once and render as Markdown while they stream, the TUI survives a slow or restarted service, /compact works on coding sessions, and the background service no longer stops right after starting on Windows installs in a virtual environment. It also includes five community fixes and dependency security updates.

Highlights

  • Answers shown once, rendered as Markdown. The TUI no longer prints an answer a second time when it finishes, and a stopped answer keeps the text already shown. Headings, lists, bold text and tables are formatted as each line completes; code blocks are not indented or wrapped by DeepCode, so they copy back exactly; links show their address; and the line still being written is previewed above the status line. /raw prints answers exactly as written. The reasoning card comes before the answer, Ctrl+O mid-answer no longer repeats or drops lines, and text such as root:x:0 or :smile: is no longer turned into emoji. See The terminal UI.
  • A TUI that keeps working. A failed request, an unrenderable event, or a restarted service no longer closes the TUI; /reconnect starts the service again when needed. Typing, completion, Enter and Ctrl+C stay responsive while the service is busy, and a slow answer is reported instead of retried three times. Esc interrupts only from an empty prompt and Ctrl+C first clears your draft, so a message you are typing is never lost or sent by accident.
  • Settings that stay current. Default model and access changes show up in the TUI, /new follows your defaults, an approval answered in another client is announced, and /goal clear out … sets a new objective instead of clearing the Goal.
  • /compact that works on coding sessions. Compaction runs in its Session's turn, so a message sent meanwhile waits for the summary and the next reply does not start with a failed request. Tool-call arguments, such as the file a write_file call carries, now count, so a session that wrote large files compacts instead of being refused as "would not shrink". A refusal says why. (#258)
  • The Windows service stays up. On a Windows install in a virtual environment, the background service stopped right after it reported ready, whichever of the TUI, deepcode service start, or deepcode web launched it. It now stays up.
  • Community fixes. Diff lines that contain a Unicode line separator or a form feed stay whole (#253); web fetch refuses private addresses tunnelled through NAT64 or IPv4-compatible IPv6 (#254); the destructive-command screen also catches absolute paths such as /bin/rm -rf / (#255); and glob finds files when the project sits under a directory named build or venv (#256).
  • Security updates. pypdf, PyJWT, urllib3, and multidict move to patched releases.

Upgrading

pip install -U deepcode-hku, then deepcode service restart so the background service runs the new version. The TUI tells you when the client and the service versions differ.

Thanks

This release includes contributions from @KennyMcSimpson, @raymondginger2018-sudo, @D41910, and @liuzhengyang699, and @raymondginger2018-sudo and @rifkir23 tracked down the cause of the failing Windows CI job. Thank you.

Full changelog: https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepCode/compare/v2.3.0...v2.3.1

DeepCode v2.3.1 是一次针对共享后台服务下终端界面的稳定性更新：回答只显示一次，并且边输出边渲染成 Markdown；后台服务变慢或重启时 TUI 照常工作；/compact 能压缩写代码的会话；在 Windows 上把 DeepCode 装在虚拟环境里时，后台服务不再刚启动就退出。本版本还包含五项社区修复和依赖的安全更新。

亮点

  • 回答只显示一次，并渲染成 Markdown。 回答结束时，TUI 不再把整段重新打印一遍；被中断的回答会保留已经输出的文字。标题、列表、粗体和表格在每行写完时排好；代码块不缩进，DeepCode 也不会给它折行，复制出来和原文一致；链接显示完整地址；还没写完的那一行先在状态行上方预览。/raw 按原文输出。推理卡片显示在回答之前；回答途中按 Ctrl+O 不会再重复或丢行；root:x:0、:smile: 这类文字不再被替换成表情。参见终端界面指南（英文）。
  • TUI 不再轻易中断。 请求失败、遇到无法显示的事件、后台服务重启，都不会再让 TUI 退出；需要时 /reconnect 会重新启动后台服务。服务忙时，打字、补全、Enter 和 Ctrl+C 照常响应；回答慢时会直接说明，不再连续重试三次。只有输入框为空时 Esc 才中断回合，Ctrl+C 先清空正在输入的内容，正在写的消息不会丢失，也不会被误发。
  • 设置及时生效。 修改默认模型或权限后，TUI 会显示最新值；/new 跟随默认设置；在其他客户端处理过的审批会有提示；/goal clear out … 会设为新目标，而不是清掉当前 Goal。
  • /compact 能压缩写代码的会话。 压缩在会话自己的回合里进行，期间发来的消息会等摘要完成，压缩后的第一次回答不再先失败一次。工具调用的参数（比如 write_file 写入的整个文件）也会计入，写过大文件的会话不再被判成"压缩后不会变小"而拒绝。被拒绝时会说明原因。（#258）
  • Windows 后台服务不再自行退出。 在 Windows 上把 DeepCode 装在虚拟环境里时，后台服务报告就绪后随即退出，无论是由 TUI、deepcode service start 还是 deepcode web 启动。现在能正常运行。
  • 社区修复。 含 Unicode 行分隔符或换页符的行在 diff 里不再被拆开（#253）；网页抓取会拒绝经 NAT64 或 IPv4 兼容 IPv6 地址访问内网（#254）；危险命令筛查也能识别 /bin/rm -rf / 这类绝对路径写法（#255）；项目放在名为 build 或 venv 的目录下时，glob 也能找到文件（#256）。
  • 安全更新。 pypdf、PyJWT、urllib3、multidict 升级到修补版本。

升级

pip install -U deepcode-hku，然后运行 deepcode service restart，让后台服务也换成新版本。客户端与后台服务版本不一致时，TUI 会提示。

致谢

本版本包含来自 @KennyMcSimpson、@raymondginger2018-sudo、@D41910 与 @liuzhengyang699 的贡献；@raymondginger2018-sudo 和 @rifkir23 还查明了 Windows CI 失败的原因。谢谢你们。

items.title: DeepCode v2.3.0
items.summary: DeepCode v2.3.0 runs the TUI, Desktop, and a new browser client on one local background service, so work you start in one interface keeps running and can be followed and approved from another. It adds voice dictation, Opper and Amazon Bedrock, correct DeepSeek…
items.html:
DeepCode v2.3.0 runs the TUI, Desktop, and a new browser client on one local background service, so work you start in one interface keeps running and can be followed and approved from another. It adds voice dictation, Opper and Amazon Bedrock, correct DeepSeek V4 numbers, and a set of opt-in protections for model traffic that passes through a relay. It also fixes a SQLite locking bug behind occasional "database disk image is malformed" errors and folds in three weeks of community work.

Highlights

  • One local service, three interfaces. deepcode, deepcode desktop, and the new deepcode web all connect to the same local background service. Closing a client leaves running work in the background; reconnect from another interface to follow the conversation and answer approvals. Model connections you save work in all three, and you can test streaming and tool calls before relying on a custom server. Manage the service with deepcode service. (#212)
  • Dictate your prompt. Add a dictation block to your config and the Desktop and Web composer gains a microphone. Speech is transcribed by a Parakeet server or the local parakeet-mlx command and inserted at the cursor for you to review. (#240)
  • More providers, truer numbers. Opper (one EU-hosted, OpenAI-compatible key for many vendors) and Amazon Bedrock join the templates, and DeepSeek V4 models use their own 1M-token window and pricing instead of V3's. (#242, #208, #249)
  • Desktop polish. Drag the conversation's edge to resize it, import a VS Code color theme, and pick from fonts that are actually installed. (#238, #207, #239)
  • Opt-in hardening for relayed model traffic. providers.egress limits which hosts receive your prompts; DEEPCODE_COMMAND_SCREEN=strict refuses piped remote scripts, unknown package indexes, and look-alike package names; DEEPCODE_BASH_SCRUB_ENV=1 keeps provider keys out of shell commands; DEEPCODE_TRANSPARENCY_LOG=1 makes the LLM log tamper-evident; DEEPCODE_KEYRING=1 reads keys from the OS keychain. All are off by default. The legacy command executor now applies the destructive-command screen as well, and each session logs its resolved permission posture. (#228–#232, #246)
  • Leaner memory, clearer signals. MEMORY.md can be a short index of topic files that the agent reads on demand, kept deduplicated and within budget; mcp list flags servers worth a second look; the agent gets a one-time reminder when a call keeps returning the same result; a misspelled tool name gets a "did you mean"; python -m core.observability.llmops summarizes cost and latency; and schedules can skip the model call when nothing they watch has changed. (#233, #241, #247, #215, #221, #227)
  • Steadier everywhere. The state database no longer drops its SQLite locks when several DeepCode processes share it; the memory data boundary now catches every spelling of its closing tag; and Windows fixes landed for GBK consoles, .git/info/exclude, private-storage permissions, and the entry point. (#243, #210, #237, #235, #236)

Upgrading

pip install -U deepcode-hku. From this release on, deepcode service prepare-upgrade --output <path> stops the background service and snapshots its state before an upgrade; see Upgrading DeepCode.

Thanks

This release includes contributions from @Dev-next-gen, @EduCosta85, @Felixkw12, @lihuiyang1024, and @raymondginger2018-sudo — thank you.

Full changelog: https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepCode/compare/v2.2.0...v2.3.0

DeepCode v2.3.0 让 TUI、Desktop 和新增的浏览器客户端共用一个本地后台服务：在一个界面里开始的任务会在后台继续运行，并能在另一个界面里跟进和审批。本版本新增语音输入、Opper 与 Amazon Bedrock 模板、正确的 DeepSeek V4 参数，以及一组针对经过中转的模型流量、需要主动开启的防护。它还修复了一个 SQLite 锁的问题（此前偶发"database disk image is malformed"错误的原因），并合入了三周来的社区贡献。

亮点

  • 一个本地服务，三种界面。 deepcode、deepcode desktop 与新增的 deepcode web 都连接同一个本地后台服务。关闭客户端后，正在运行的工作留在后台；从另一个界面重新连接，即可继续跟进对话、回应审批。保存的模型连接在三种界面通用，使用自定义服务前可以先测试流式输出与工具调用。用 deepcode service 管理后台服务。（#212）
  • 用语音输入提示词。 在配置中加入 dictation 后，Desktop 与 Web 的输入框会出现麦克风。语音由 Parakeet 服务或本地 parakeet-mlx 命令转写，插入到光标处，发送前可以检查修改。（#240）
  • 更多服务商，更准的参数。 新增 Opper（用一个托管在欧盟的 OpenAI-compatible 密钥调用多家厂商的模型）与 Amazon Bedrock 模板；DeepSeek V4 使用自己的 100 万上下文与价格，不再沿用 V3 的数值。（#242、#208、#249）
  • Desktop 细节打磨。 拖动会话区边缘即可调宽，可以导入 VS Code 配色主题，字体选择只列出本机已安装的字体。（#238、#207、#239）
  • 可选的中转流量加固。 providers.egress 限定哪些主机能收到你的提示词；DEEPCODE_COMMAND_SCREEN=strict 拒绝下载后直接执行的远程脚本、未知的包索引和仿冒包名；DEEPCODE_BASH_SCRUB_ENV=1 不把服务商密钥交给 shell 命令；DEEPCODE_TRANSPARENCY_LOG=1 让 LLM 日志可以校验是否被篡改；DEEPCODE_KEYRING=1 从系统钥匙串读取密钥。以上默认全部关闭。另外，旧版命令执行器也会先经过危险命令筛查，每个 Session 会在日志里记录最终生效的权限状态。（#228–#232、#246）
  • 更轻的记忆，更清楚的提示。 MEMORY.md 可以只是一份主题文件索引，由 Agent 按需读取，并保持去重、不超预算；mcp list 会标出值得再看一眼的 server；同一调用反复返回相同结果时，Agent 会收到一次提醒；工具名写错时会提示"是否想用"；python -m core.observability.llmops 汇总成本与延迟；定时任务在监视的内容没有变化时可以跳过模型调用。（#233、#241、#247、#215、#221、#227）
  • 各平台更稳定。 多个 DeepCode 进程共用状态数据库时不再丢失 SQLite 锁；记忆的数据边界能识别结束标签的各种写法；Windows 上修复了 GBK 控制台、.git/info/exclude、私有存储权限与入口文件的问题。（#243、#210、#237、#235、#236）

升级

pip install -U deepcode-hku。从本版本起，升级前可以用 deepcode service prepare-upgrade --output <路径> 停下后台服务并为状态做快照，详见升级指南（英文）。

致谢

本版本包含来自 @Dev-next-gen、@EduCosta85、@Felixkw12、@lihuiyang1024 与 @raymondginger2018-sudo 的贡献——谢谢你们。

items.title: DeepCode v2.2.0
items.summary: DeepCode v2.2.0 makes long sessions dependable and puts the model under your control: sessions survive resume, compaction, and a second window; settings, models, and reasoning are declared rather than guessed; sub-agents and MCP servers start when needed and…
items.html:
DeepCode v2.2.0 makes long sessions dependable and puts the model under your control: sessions survive resume, compaction, and a second window; settings, models, and reasoning are declared rather than guessed; sub-agents and MCP servers start when needed and stop cleanly; and the Desktop speaks Simplified Chinese. It also folds in a month of community fixes and security hardening.

Highlights

  • Sessions that hold up. Resuming a session restores what the agent did, not only what it said; compaction keeps the recent tail and can be triggered on demand with /compact; context pressure is measured from the provider's own usage; and two windows on one session no longer crash each other — one live writer per session, enforced.
  • Your models, declared. A dsh-style settings dialog with per-model declarations (context window, capacities, reasoning ladder), live model discovery per connection, a Session-level context-window cap (/context 64k), and keys that reach exactly the requests they were resolved for.
  • A terminal that reads like an app. Every bare command opens a selector, the TUI has a status line and tool cards, and a new turn no longer discards the prompt cache.
  • Sub-agents and MCP, on demand. Delegate to Codex or Claude Code as sub-agents, hold follow-up conversations with native ones, activate MCP servers lazily, and let hooks see the whole lifecycle (SessionEnd, PreCompact).
  • Memory with boundaries. Compaction leaves a note in workspace memory, and injected memory content sits inside an escaped <untrusted-data> boundary, so a poisoned note cannot forge instructions.
  • Desktop in Simplified Chinese, eight themes including a high-contrast one, an appearance scale that actually resizes the app, and a project switch that no longer strands the MCP catalog.
  • Hardening. Command-executor bypasses closed, native file operations routed through the sandbox, Windows private files protected by a fail-safe ACL, Plugin manifests warned about plaintext credentials, and dependency advisories (pip, pypdf, browserslist) cleared.

Thanks

This release includes contributions from @atirna, @lihuiyang1024, @rifkir23, @MarkHe1222, @imshunsuke, and @raymondginger2018-sudo — thank you.

Full changelog: https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepCode/compare/v2.1.0...v2.2.0

DeepCode v2.2.0 让长会话变得可靠，并把模型真正交到你手里：Session 经得住恢复、压缩和第二个窗口；设置、模型与推理档位改为显式声明而非猜测；子代理与 MCP 服务器按需启动、干净退出；Desktop 说简体中文。同时合入了一个月的社区修复与安全加固。

亮点

  • 站得住的 Session。 恢复会话时找回的是 Agent 做过什么而不只是说过什么；压缩保留最近的尾部，也可用 /compact 按需触发；上下文压力按服务商报告的真实用量测量；同一 Session 开两个窗口不再互相崩溃——每个 Session 只有一个活跃写入者，由系统锁保证。
  • 你的模型，显式声明。 dsh 风格的设置对话框，逐模型声明（上下文窗口、容量、推理档位），每个连接可实时发现模型，Session 级上下文上限（/context 64k），密钥只到达为它解析的请求。
  • 像应用而不是日志的终端。 每个裸命令都打开选择器，TUI 有状态行与工具卡片，新的 Turn 不再丢掉提示缓存。
  • 按需的子代理与 MCP。 可把任务委派给 Codex 或 Claude Code 子代理，与原生子代理进行后续对话，MCP 服务器懒启动，Hooks 看得到完整生命周期（SessionEnd、PreCompact）。
  • 有边界的记忆。 压缩会在工作区记忆里留下一条笔记；注入的记忆内容包在转义过的 <untrusted-data> 边界里，被投毒的笔记无法伪造指令。
  • 简体中文的 Desktop，八套主题（含高对比度），真正缩放整个应用的字号偏好，以及切换项目不再让 MCP 目录卡住。
  • 安全加固。 堵上命令执行器的绕过，原生文件操作走沙箱，Windows 私有文件获得 fail-safe 的 ACL，插件清单对明文凭据发出警告，并清除了 pip、pypdf、browserslist 的依赖公告。

致谢

本版本包含来自 @atirna、@lihuiyang1024、@rifkir23、@MarkHe1222、@imshunsuke 与 @raymondginger2018-sudo 的贡献——谢谢你们。

items.title: DeepCode v2.0.0
items.summary: After continuous iteration, HKUDS DeepCode v2 is officially released 🚀 An open-source, general-purpose Coding Agent built for real-world software engineering. Coding Agents are becoming increasingly capable of generating high-quality code. However, developers…
items.html:
After continuous iteration, HKUDS DeepCode v2 is officially released 🚀 An open-source, general-purpose Coding Agent built for real-world software engineering.

Coding Agents are becoming increasingly capable of generating high-quality code. However, developers still face several recurring problems in real projects:

  • ⏸️ Complex tasks stop halfway and require repeated prompts to continue
  • 🧪 Code appears complete, but tests, builds, and runtime behavior are not actually verified
  • 🔁 Regression checks, test repairs, documentation updates, and repository maintenance must be initiated manually each time

DeepCode v2 is designed to reduce this repeated communication and manual work.

Instead of only generating code, it helps developers continuously move tasks forward inside real repositories until the results are verified and ready for review.

What is new in DeepCode v2:

  • 🔄 Loop Engineering DeepCode continuously understands, implements, verifies, and repairs work around a natural-language Goal. It does not stop after producing a single response, but keeps progressing based on real execution results.

  • 🎛️ Control throughout execution Developers can add requirements, revise the Goal, pause, resume, or change direction while the Agent is running, without losing work that has already been completed.

  • ✅ Verified delivery DeepCode actually runs commands, tests, and builds, and delivers results together with code changes and execution evidence, making them easier to review, validate, and merge.

  • 🤖 Personalized Automation Developers can create project-specific tasks using natural language and run them manually or on a schedule for regression checks, test repairs, documentation synchronization, and repository maintenance.

  • 💻 Unified CLI and Desktop experience The same project, Session, Goal, and execution history can be continued across both CLI and Desktop, reducing context loss when switching tools.

We hope DeepCode v2 helps open-source developers and engineering teams spend more time on meaningful design, decision-making, and creation—and less time repeatedly prompting Agents, rechecking results, or explaining the same task again.

Less prompting. More completed work.

Try DeepCode v2, share your feedback, open an Issue, or join us in building it together. 🚀

items.html:
DeepCode v1.3.0 完成了 V2 架构升级，将 DeepCode 扩展为更统一、安全且可扩展的通用智能编程代理。

  • 统一 CLI、Web 与 Headless 模式的 Agent 内核和事件协议，同时保留原有 Paper2Code 工作流。
  • 新增交互式 CLI、原生编程工具、持久化 Session、项目记忆与长对话上下文管理。
  • 引入权限控制、安全沙箱、工具审批及工作区隔离机制。
  • 支持自主循环、定时任务、并行团队与模型驱动的子代理协作。
  • 支持 Skills、生命周期 Hooks、分层配置，以及在任意目录中启动和恢复 DeepCode。

DeepCode v1.3.0 delivers the V2 architecture upgrade, evolving DeepCode into a more unified, secure, and extensible general-purpose coding agent.

  • Unified the agent runtime and event protocol across CLI, Web, and headless modes while preserving the existing Paper2Code workflow.
  • Added an interactive CLI, native coding tools, persistent sessions, project memory, and long-context management.
  • Introduced permission controls, security sandboxing, tool approvals, and workspace isolation.
  • Added autonomous loops, scheduled tasks, parallel teams, and model-driven subagent collaboration.
  • Added Skills, lifecycle Hooks, layered configuration, and support for launching and resuming DeepCode from any directory.

New Version:

  1. We have updated DeepCode’s overall workflow and fixed several issues and bugs previously reported by users.

  2. We have improved the robustness of the system and introduced targeted optimizations for models with relatively weaker coding capabilities.

  3. Our currently recommended most stable and high‑quality large language models include: Claude 3.5 and above, GPT‑4o and above, and Gemini‑pro.

  4. We will continue to iterate, further refining the workflow and robustness, and adapting the system for stable operation across multiple model families. Future roadmap:

  5. DeepCode will release related technical reports.

  6. We will launch automated code verification and execution features.

  7. We will keep iterating and advancing the system through continuous technological innovation and adoption.

新版本：

  1. 我们已对 DeepCode 的整体 workflow 进行了更新，修复了此前大家反馈的一些问题和 Bug。
  2. 提升了模型的鲁棒性，并针对部分代码能力相对较弱的模型进行了专项优化。
  3. 当前推荐使用的最稳定且高质量的大语言模型包括：Claude 3.5 及以上版本、GPT‑4o 及以上版本，以及 Gemini‑pro。
  4. 我们将持续迭代，进一步优化 workflow 与鲁棒性，并针对多种模型进行稳定性适配。

未来规划：

  1. DeepCode 将发布相关技术报告；
  2. 上线代码自动化验证与执行功能；
  3. 持续迭代升级，引入和落地更多前沿技术。

items.title: DeepCode v1.0.5
items.summary: Got a brilliant idea in mind but don’t know where to start? It’s time to let the Agent become your product manager! DeepCode Major Update! We are introducing a brand-new personalized requirements customization feature. It’s a new interactive feature that turns…
items.html:
Got a brilliant idea in mind but don’t know where to start? It’s time to let the Agent become your product manager! DeepCode Major Update! We are introducing a brand-new personalized requirements customization feature.

It’s a new interactive feature that turns vague ideas into actionable development plans. Instead of requiring you to provide detailed specifications up front, DeepCode’s Agent will:

  • Ask clarifying questions about your idea.
  • Break down abstract requirements into concrete functional specifications.
  • Continuously refine and optimize the plan based on your additional input.
  • Adapt dynamically until the final plan matches exactly what you need.

From a single sentence to a complete project blueprint—experience the magic of co-creating with AI right now! This update also brings a brand-new UI with a smoother and more intuitive experience. Coming soon, we’ll add powerful features like automated testing and performance dashboards. But this is just the beginning. Our roadmap includes even more exciting features:

Automated Verification and Optimization Agents: automated testing, sandbox verification, and a more comprehensive coding experience.

Benchmark Dashboards: detailed performance metrics on the PaperBench evaluation suite to stay transparent and ahead.

System-Wide Optimizations: stronger reasoning and broader multi-language framework support.

We are building the future of software development—stay tuned! Try it now: https://github.com/HKUDS/DeepCode

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.323
items.summary: What's changed Added Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools; see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode to turn it on, or to turn it off for an organization Added engines["claude-code"] to plugin.json: plugins…
items.html:
What's changed

  • Added Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools; see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode to turn it on, or to turn it off for an organization
  • Added engines["claude-code"] to plugin.json: plugins outside their stated Claude Code version range are not installed, updated or loaded, and install and update pick the newest version that fits
  • Added type checking of a plugin's TypeScript hooks module to claude plugin validate; each finding is a warning, and --strict fails on it
  • Added to claude plugin validate the $ nouns a mod's engine.create hook adds, withholds or replaces
  • Added support for CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL in managed settings for Claude Desktop sessions on third-party providers (takes effect once Claude Desktop includes this version)
  • Added an options menu (stop, switch to usage credits, upgrade) when a model needs usage credits that are turned off or used up
  • Added a progress heartbeat every 30 seconds while hooks run long in claude -p and SDK sessions, so a host such as Claude Desktop won't end the turn as hung (once it includes this version)
  • Added .docx support to Artifact tool asset uploads
  • Added a /diff to close hint to the diff panel, and the keys that focus and close a panel to the ? shortcut guide
  • Added a start-up warning for Bash allow rules with a * in a variable's value, such as Bash(PORT=* npm run dev)
  • Added a warning when a plugin's language server can't start, naming the server and what to check
  • Added a one-time startup notice naming CLAUDE_CODE_PERFORCE_MODE when Perforce settings are found and the mode is off
  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_PROGRESS_SUMMARIES (available since 2.1.318): set it to 1 to turn off subagent progress summaries and the requests that write them (anthropics/claude-code#86879)
  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_HINT_COMMAND, which a program that starts Claude Code can set to have the exit hint name its own resume command
  • Added unsetOptionCount to the claude plugin install --json result: how many userConfig options are not yet set
  • Added isPromptCovered to the props a mod's pane is drawn with, telling it when a dialog or a field above the prompt covers the prompt
  • Fixed running /compact again, or after a command such as /context, summarizing away a message that Claude had not answered yet
  • Fixed a resumed session joining your next message to an old interrupted message that was not resumed
  • Fixed a memory spike at the next prompt after Claude changed a very large file
  • Fixed a setting saved in a running session undoing a hand edit made to settings.json moments earlier; a settings file you delete during a session now stays deleted
  • Fixed claude plugin commands and claude mcp list signing you out of a Console profile when they ended while the token was being renewed
  • Fixed Edit and Bash running out of memory on certain /proc files, and Edit hanging or running out of memory on devices and named pipes
  • Fixed Claude Code failing to start, or to clear stored credentials at sign-out, when saving its configuration file failed with "Out of memory"
  • Fixed requests sent without streaming failing on errors that streamed requests recover from, such as a rejected image, thinking block or beta header
  • Fixed ExitWorktree, the worktree exit dialog and /resume leaving the session in the wrong folder when the folder the shell was in before entering the worktree had been deleted
  • Fixed accents and other combining marks sometimes landing left of the text, leaving stale copies on screen, or silently disappearing when text wraps
  • Fixed the last key of a key chord, such as Enter in ctrl+x enter, acting on a dialog's text field when the chord's own action isn't available there
  • Fixed ps processes piling up when the process listing Claude Code runs before stopping a command takes too long
  • Fixed subagent transcripts and large tool results being saved apart from the session's transcript after entering a worktree created by a WorktreeCreate hook or belonging to a nested repository
  • Fixed a session on a named Anthropic profile moving to another sign-in when /fork, the Left arrow or --bg continued it in the background; reopen any session that was open during the update
  • Fixed a background session sending a conversation under another sign-in when its named Anthropic profile is missing, changed or overridden; it now stops and says so
  • Fixed a session on an API key, auth token or workload identity from its shell (not a setup token) moving to another sign-in in the background; it now stops and says so
  • Fixed MCP tool calls ending in the sign-in server's error, such as TOKEN_EXPIRED, instead of asking you to sign in again
  • Fixed an expired claude.ai login showing "Credit balance too low" when a saved Console key or ant auth login profile without credit was used instead
  • Fixed a session on a named Anthropic profile being handed to an older background service that could not keep its sign-in; it now says to restart the service
  • Fixed a background session's sign-in leaving the previous account's login or other credentials in place; it now clears them for every session on the computer, and a refused sign-in can leave no login
  • Fixed background sessions moving between a profile and the stored login when an update restarted them
  • Fixed sessions opened before a sign-in keeping signed-out feature flags after the sign-in
  • Fixed sessions that kept failing after a Claude apps gateway sign-in expired: once you sign in again with /login in another terminal, they carry on at the next message
  • Fixed the billing notice naming your ant auth login organization when a custom X-Api-Key header is set
  • macOS: Fixed "Not logged in · Please run /login" coming back right after a successful /login or a token refresh when the keychain was slow to answer
  • Fixed turns failing in Claude Desktop when an organization's gateway answers an expired token with 403: Claude Code now asks Desktop for a fresh token and retries
  • Fixed the error shown when Amazon Bedrock refuses your account a model: it no longer says to refresh your AWS credentials, it says to enable the model
  • Fixed the awsAuthRefresh or gcpAuthRefresh command sometimes running twice for one request when three or more sessions needed a fresh sign-in at once
  • Fixed the claude -p warning about an ended claude.ai login to say that claude auth logout also removes saved MCP server logins and plugin secrets
  • Fixed Bash permission prompts offering "don't ask again" for commands that write to sensitive paths such as .git or .claude, where the saved rule did not stop the next prompt
  • Fixed a case where some lsof commands ran without a permission prompt
  • Fixed Bash commands that write a file with cat > file <<EOF being shown as "Read 1 file"
  • Fixed a case where Bash permission checks judged an rm from the wrong folder and skipped the dangerous-removal prompt under bypass permissions or a Bash allow rule
  • Fixed --permission-mode auto or a settings defaultMode: auto starting in a mode that could allow more when auto mode was unavailable. It now starts in Manual mode, which asks first
  • Fixed plan files sometimes being written outside the project when plansDirectory is set; a write that can't be shown to stay inside the project is now refused
  • Fixed a permission prompt when Claude read the output of its own background command or agent after entering a worktree
  • Fixed a case where Bash permission checks missed part of a command
  • Fixed a case where the Bash sandbox could switch off during a session
  • Fixed Bash allow rules with an attached wildcard, such as Bash(ls*), skipping the permission prompt in some cases; a rule that names a variable, such as Bash(NODE_ENV*), now asks
  • Fixed auto mode running behind a gateway at ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL

…

items.summary: What's changed Added Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2), now the default Fable model — 1M context, $8/$40 per Mtok with $0.20/Mtok cache reads Added --settings <file> to claude remote-control, which applies a settings file to every session it starts; if the…
items.html:
What's changed

  • Added Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2), now the default Fable model — 1M context, $8/$40 per Mtok with $0.20/Mtok cache reads
  • Added --settings <file> to claude remote-control, which applies a settings file to every session it starts; if the file changes, no new session starts until you restart claude remote-control
  • Fixed MCP OAuth requests sending secrets such as refresh tokens to another host when a server redirected them
  • Fixed a case where a read-only Bash command ran outside the sandbox without a permission prompt
  • Fixed a case where Bash permission checks judged a file write from the wrong folder and didn't prompt
  • Fixed deny rules and protected-file prompts not applying to the file that a cp or mv into a directory writes
  • Fixed the "Draws from usage credits" note showing after a switch to Fable on Enterprise seats whose plan includes Fable
  • Fixed the fallback model sometimes declining a request or mentioning a stopped response when the first model was blocked before replying
  • Fixed claude mcp login printing a SEP-2352 issuer warning each time you sign in again to a server that Claude Code registered with
  • Fixed NotebookEdit deleting or overwriting a notebook's first cell when the call named no cell, on network paths (UNC shares, WSL folders, /net mounts)
  • Fixed Edit changing the first of several matches, replacing a whole file on an empty old_string, or editing a notebook as text, on network paths (UNC shares, WSL folders, /net mounts)
  • Fixed /config showing Manual as the default permission mode when new sessions start in auto mode; pressing Space on "Auto (default)" now saves Don't Ask, not Plan
  • Windows: Fixed FileChanged hooks stopping for paths set through watchPaths after the first shell command, when the session's working directory had a lowercase drive letter
  • Fixed --plugin-dir . and --plugin-dir ./builtin writing generated type files for Claude Code's built-in plugins into a builtin folder
  • Fixed context usage estimates overcounting tool definitions when exact token counts are unavailable
  • Fixed /compact showing twice in Remote Control on web and mobile
  • Fixed plugin auto-updates and /plugin marketplace updates downloading a plugin again for each worktree or folder of a repository
  • Fixed auto mode losing a background subagent's report that had started a turn when the conversation was compacted before Claude answered it
  • Fixed project skills, commands and agents staying missing after their folder was removed and came back mid-session, such as with git stash, including after entering a worktree
  • Fixed claude -p sometimes telling Claude that background commands get 30 minutes when they are stopped after 10
  • Fixed pkill, pgrep and pidwait in cloud sessions matching the session's own parent processes
  • Fixed Claude in Chrome and computer use server processes staying alive after their parent exits behind a proxy that stalls connections
  • Fixed a large hook output pointing Claude to a file that held another hook's output from the same tool call
  • Fixed apps that embed Claude Code getting their own PreToolUse hook's ask reason instead of another hook's when both asked
  • Fixed a PreToolUse hook's ask being lost when another hook's defer finished first and could not be honored
  • Fixed a rare crash on permission prompts and background tasks
  • Fixed project skills, commands and agents disappearing from the menu in SDK and desktop sessions after Claude entered a worktree
  • Fixed /desktop on macOS saying Claude Desktop is not installed when it is in ~/Applications
  • Fixed OpenTelemetry repository attributes (vcs.*) missing from Claude Desktop sessions that start on a pre-started process
  • Fixed WebFetch passing "No response from model" to Claude as page content when the model reading the page returned no text; the call now fails with a clear error
  • Fixed screen reader mode delaying the prompt at startup when the system clock moved back while Claude Code was starting
  • Fixed a command's panel sometimes not coming back after a dialog closed, leaving no panel or prompt on screen until the next redraw
  • Fixed a project's MCP server being disconnected after the first message in a Claude Desktop Code tab session when the desktop app has an MCP server or extension of the same name
  • Fixed a turn ending with "API Error: EPROTO: The TLS handshake failed" when the connection broke partway through a reply; the partial reply is kept or the request is retried, as before 2.1.302
  • Fixed high memory use in long sessions that repeatedly read single lines from large files
  • Fixed fast mode losing replies, switching models or retrying for minutes when fast serving is rate-limited, overloaded or failing; it now tries standard speed on the same model first
  • Fixed one request carrying far more background agent reports than intended after Claude was stopped while several were waiting
  • Fixed messages from a Claude Desktop Code tab session to your other sessions staying paused after you typed while Claude was still working
  • Fixed claude agents ignoring --permission-mode, --dangerously-skip-permissions, --model, --effort or --agent typed before agents when a flag such as --verbose was also on the line
  • Fixed a case where Remote Control showed as off with "login expired" in the desktop app while its connection was still up, because the app was briefly unable to hand over a sign-in token
  • Fixed a Remote Control message sent with "Queue for later" reaching Claude in the middle of the running turn
  • Fixed the git status given to Claude at session start reading as clean when git status failed; it now reads as unavailable
  • Fixed the git status given to Claude at session start showing the first listed file as staged when its changes were not staged
  • Fixed a hang or out-of-memory crash when a connector in a cloud session lists resources with very long names
  • Fixed Remote Control showing as connected after its connection closed for good while the session's history was still uploading
  • Fixed screen reader mode turning off when you return to a conversation from agent view
  • Fixed screen reader mode y/n questions taking as yes a stray "y" at the end of text typed as the question opened
  • Fixed cloud sessions telling Claude that a host is probably not allowed when it is allowed and the network proxy could not connect to it
  • Fixed an MCP server sometimes showing as connected with no tools after it was reconnected or the session's directory changed while its tools were still loading
  • Fixed Bash commands sometimes running in the wrong folder when Claude sent several at once and an earlier one changed folders
  • Fixed files Claude sends from cloud and Remote Control sessions failing at once when an upload gets an HTTP 507 from a proxy; the upload now gets a second try
  • Fixed new messages not being saved, and claude -p, SDK and VS Code sessions hanging, when memory ran out while the transcript was being read
  • Fixed sign-in, token refresh and logout waiting indefinitely when something on the network accepts the connection but never answers the TLS handshake
  • Fixed a sent file showing under a different name in the Claude apps when its name hid text-direction or control characters; Claude now refuses to send such a file
  • Fixed sub-agent progress summaries running a request to its end after the model replied with a tool call
  • Fixed Bash reads such as grep -r foo "$PWD/src" asking for permission when the same command with the path typed out runs without asking
  • Fixed Claude apps gateway refusing to start when a desktop setting holds a field newer than the gateway, such as a managed MCP server's oauth.omitResource; it now warns and serves it
  • Fixed Bash commands coming back empty for zsh users whose .zshrc sets KSH_OPTION_PRINT
  • macOS: Fixed "Unable to read managed policy settings" at startup when a valid MDM profile was slow to read: the read is retried once, and a timeout is now reported as a timeout
