items.html:
VS Code

7.6.0

Minor Changes

  • #13951 492a2ff - Ask the agent to commit and push when you send pull request CI failures or review comments from the Agent Manager PR panel, or update a worktree from its base, so the pull request updates without a follow-up prompt. Permission prompts still confirm each commit and push. Turn off "Push Pull Request Fixes" in Settings, Agent Behaviour to keep commits manual.

  • #13927 ed3cdc6 - Add the /caffeinate command and notifications that explain when Kilo keeps the computer awake while agents work.

  • #13929 9dae829 Thanks @WebReflection! - Add an opt-in, one-time import of supported global Claude Code instructions, simple skills, and disabled MCP definitions into Kilo.

  • #13965 6bbe6ac - Click the thinking indicator to scroll the current chat to the latest message.

  • #13903 99eab84 - Write and preview multiline PR comments and code suggestions, reply from the PR panel or diff view, and edit or delete your own comments directly in Agent Manager.

    Comment on selected PR diff lines, submit reviews, and preview and apply suggested changes to the local worktree without staging, committing, or pushing.

  • #13771 3c28e7a Thanks @sylwester-liljegren! - Alert you when Kilo finishes a task, needs your input, needs permission, or hits a terminal error. Enable VS Code notifications, native OS notifications (Windows, macOS, and Linux), or both — OS notifications reach you while the editor is in the background, and VS Code notifications wait for you with a Show action that opens the session and jumps to the latest message. Notifications are skipped for the session you are already looking at, they follow your selected language, and a Test button confirms native notifications work on your system.

  • #13958 4c2a6eb - Show commits, force pushes, merges, approvals, and the pull request description in the Agent Manager PR conversation, in the order they happened.

  • #13953 3c04a86 - Show pull request approvals and merge readiness in Agent Manager, with GitHub-backed branch updates, merge methods, auto-merge, and conflict resolution with Kilo.

  • #13679 e27ff0a - Keep working toward a session goal with /goal, with shared pause, resume, and clear controls in the terminal and VS Code. Pause goals after no-action replies, terminal failures, Stop, new messages, and backend restarts. Rename custom commands or MCP prompts named goal to use this reserved command. Show a labeled Goal icon with hover details while work runs.

    Compose multiline goals with images and file attachments in VS Code. Select /goal to enter goal mode, or cancel to keep the draft as ordinary chat. Keep drafts and attachments when submission fails.

    Keep the current goal running when replacement attachments are invalid. Make pending Goal submissions read-only, and preserve the draft when Cancel exits Goal mode before acknowledgement.

    Disable clarification questions during active goals and delegated work while keeping permission approvals unchanged. Make safe, reversible decisions autonomously and report completion or blockers.

    Retain Active, Complete, Blocked, and Paused goals with their objective and reason until explicitly cleared. Let the working model explicitly report completion or a blocker with the Goal-only reporting tool, without a separate evaluator or independent verification claim. Pause no-action turns that have no explicit report. Keep complete goals complete after a backend restart and label their resume action as Restart.

    Starting a Goal while a response is running replaces that response after the Goal request is validated.

  • #13940 b8fe009 - Identify subagents with consistent theme-colored avatars in Task cards, background agents, subagent tabs, and swarm messages. Show all participants in board message headers, and animate running avatars instead of showing a separate loading indicator.

  • #13782 4d2d800 - View and reset the shared agent board from its owning session without stopping agents or clearing conversations.

Patch Changes

  • #13926 818d31d - Explain that Agent Manager requires a specific project folder when the VS Code workspace is the home folder or a filesystem root.

  • #13975 e85805f - Keep the Agent Manager PR push toggle synchronized with the Settings value across open Kilo views.

  • #13916 1ec6268 - Regroup the Agent Manager toolbar: optional session panels (documents, subagents) sit left of a separator, and the fixed workbench (changes, PR, apply, open in VS Code, browser, run, terminal) keeps stable positions on the right. Toolbar icons render at a uniform 1px stroke and dim when disabled. Open the full-screen review from the changes panel header instead of a toolbar button.

  • #13990 7febec5 - Report the direct recipient execution state in board_post results and warn when that recipient stopped, failed, was cancelled, or is unknown, so agents do not assume a finished subagent will read the message.

  • #13967 0aad88e - Resolve agent board route metadata from the session store while a message is still being written, so sender and recipient avatars and titles appear without waiting for the completed tool result.

  • #13920 05c763f - Show an actionable message when creating worktrees from a repository with no commits.

items.html:
Fixed

  • Restore CLI and TUI startup after v7.5.0 could open to a black screen on Windows and macOS.
  • Fix the Windows startup failure caused by Bun 1.4 raising EACCES while probing WindowsApps\pwsh.exe.
  • Restore the proven Bun 1.3.14 runtime and non-split compiled CLI configuration from v7.4.23.
  • Ship the corrected CLI in the npm package and all stable VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX platform builds.

This release supersedes v7.5.0.

Upgrade

npm install -g @kilocode/cli@latest
kilo --version

The reported version should be 7.5.4. VS Code installations receive the corrected extension through the normal stable update channel.

Validation

  • Built and validated all CLI release targets.
  • Passed artifact smoke tests on Windows x64/arm64, macOS x64/arm64, Linux x64/arm64, and Alpine x64/arm64.
  • Passed the end-to-end pre-publish agent smoke gate.

Fixes #13467 and #13473. Implemented in #13481.

items.html:
7.4.22

Minor Changes

  • #11219 8013e5f Thanks @sylwester-liljegren! - Make file references in agent responses clickable by validating inline code spans against the filesystem. Code spans that match real files in the workspace become clickable links that open the file at the referenced line. Non-existent paths stay as plain code. Also adds fallback workspace search and "File not found" warning when clicking dead links.

  • #13071 3e3dd3d Thanks @cosi-conda! - Add Agent Manager PR comment actions: resolve/unresolve review threads, jump to comments section, and scroll-to-top for PR diff view.

  • #13084 5c97b48 - Remove the built-in experimental Morph WarpGrep codebase search tool and ignore its retired configuration flag.

Patch Changes

  • #13063 ca9a99f - Show and select the model's default reasoning variant in chat and Agent Manager.

  • #13100 753d560 - Support structured AWS access keys and Google Cloud service-account JSON when connecting Bedrock and Vertex AI in VS Code.

  • #12373 3a99f36 Thanks @mvanhorn! - Fix subagent permission errors that referenced phantom deny rules and blocked commands the subagent's own config explicitly allowed. A read-only or delegating agent's readOnlyBash allowlist is no longer projected onto a writable subagent as a bash ceiling, so a delegated subagent can run its own allowed commands (e.g. git status). Edit, notebook, and MCP denials are still inherited as hard ceilings.

  • #13088 9f4ab3a - Keep the Changes chip and Git changes visible across tab switches in multi-repository workspaces.

  • Changes from opencode v1.17.13 to v1.18.0 upstream:

    • Core Improvements: Added a code mode MCP adapter for running confined orchestration scripts against connected MCP tools.
    • Core Improvements: Hid the execute tool unless code mode is enabled.
    • Core Improvements: Add a model-specific system prompt for Meta Muse Spark.
    • Core Improvements: Updated Azure AI support for GPT-5.6.
    • Core Bugfixes: Fixed paginated MCP tool catalogs losing tool metadata and output schema validation.
    • Core Bugfixes: Preserved low reasoning effort for OpenRouter small-model variants instead of disabling it.
    • Core Bugfixes: Fixed GitHub Copilot model routing to honor each model's advertised chat or responses endpoint.
    • Core Bugfixes: Fixed session lists to match equivalent instance directories reliably.
    • Core Bugfixes: Fixed Cerebras reasoning replay so earlier assistant reasoning is sent back in the provider-supported field.
    • Core Bugfixes: Better classify Z.ai context-window overflow errors so oversized requests surface the right failure mode (@fengjikui)
    • Core Bugfixes: Handle unavailable config directories more gracefully when reading config files
    • Core Bugfixes: Exposed reasoning effort variants for Grok models.
    • Core Bugfixes: Improved xAI prompt cache routing and PDF file support in Responses models.
    • Core Bugfixes: Improved Meta model handling for reasoning variants and provider requests.
    • Core Bugfixes: Prevent crashes and bad pricing data when GitHub Copilot returns models with a zero billing batch size.
    • Core Bugfixes: Supported OpenAI pro reasoning mode.
    • Core Bugfixes: Disabled response storage by default for xAI Responses. (@geraint0923)
    • Core Bugfixes: Added OAuth support for Luna Responses Lite.
    • Core Bugfixes: Switched to another available org after logging out in the console.
    • Core Bugfixes: Used Codex context limits for GPT-5.6 over OAuth. (@nabilfreeman)
    • Core Bugfixes: Removed an obsolete Codex workaround that could interfere with OpenAI Luna Responses Lite requests.
    • TUI Bugfixes: Fixed spinner registration so loading indicators keep rendering across TUI surfaces.

Minor Changes

Cmd+/ now focuses a visible embedded terminal before hiding it, Cmd+Shift+T creates a side terminal only while that terminal area has focus, and Cmd+Shift+[ / ] switch terminal tabs. Cmd+Shift+M focuses the Agent Manager prompt instead of opening VS Code Problems. Cmd+W hides the last side terminal instead of stopping its shell.

  • #12865 35801cb - Prevent VS Code sessions and Agent Manager worktrees from starting unused file watchers and defer file indexing until search is used.

  • #12983 40121d8 - Compress speech-to-text audio input to AAC format across macOS, Linux, and Windows to prevent payload size errors on long recordings.

  • #12979 0485e36 - Start Agent Manager worktree sessions faster by prefetching base branches, reducing workspace file-watcher load, and overlapping independent multi-session setup.

  • #12958 fdc4665 - Reduce noisy memory timeout warnings and retry transient background consolidation failures once.

items.summary: 7.4.18 Minor Changes #12681 3ab1122 - Add a scope selector and base branch picker to the Agent Manager diff review. The side panel and full-screen review now let you switch between Branch, Staged, Unstaged, and Session scopes for the selected worktree, and the…
items.html:
7.4.18

Minor Changes

  • #12681 3ab1122 - Add a scope selector and base branch picker to the Agent Manager diff review. The side panel and full-screen review now let you switch between Branch, Staged, Unstaged, and Session scopes for the selected worktree, and the Branch scope's base branch can be overridden from a picker next to it. Branch stays the default, so existing review behavior is unchanged.

  • #12566 46b7e55 - Add an experimental multi-project foundation for Agent Manager behind the Multi-Project Agent Manager toggle in Kilo Settings > Experimental. A persistent project registry catalogs additional Git repositories across restarts while the current workspace repository stays the pinned default project, and all repository-bound services (state, worktrees, setup scripts, stale tracking, polling) are now owned by immutable per-project contexts that can be activated, expanded, and switched through new project protocol messages. Every expanded project runs its own git stats and PR pollers, so all visible project accordions show live data at the same time; switching projects keeps previously visited projects expanded and restores the exact worktree or session that was open there. Sessions created anywhere (sidebar, another window, the CLI) appear in the owning project's list immediately, and open tabs stay private to the project they were opened in. Single-project behavior is unchanged when the experiment is disabled.

  • #12709 5c140b1 - Make the Agent Manager diff review follow the sidebar selection instead of a single session. Switching session tabs inside a worktree no longer refetches the Branch, Staged, and Unstaged scopes, the Session scope now swaps to the active session's changes on tab switch, and the Local tab gains the Session scope so sessions running in the workspace can be reviewed on their own. The Session scope shows a notice when snapshots are disabled instead of a blank list, worktrees without an open session now still show their branch diff, and the Apply dialog lists the worktree's changes again.

  • #12680 49223b3 - Run Agent Manager project scripts in the terminal selected by the existing toolbar dropdown. Agent Manager panel uses the named side terminal, while VS Code terminal retains the integrated task flow.

  • #12424 d6380b2 Thanks @bsflasher! - Add Persian (Farsi) as a UI language, including right-to-left layout. Contributed by Babak Safabahar.

  • #12606 286b672 Thanks @bagatao-anaconda! - Show skill shell commands in the permission prompt. When a skill runs embedded shell commands, the approval dialog now lists every command with Allow / Reject.

  • #12703 5076b62 - Run Agent Manager worktree setup scripts in the terminal selected by the toolbar dropdown. Agent Manager panel shows live setup output in a named Setup side tab that reveals itself while provisioning and hides again on success unless you engaged with the panel, while VS Code terminal retains the integrated task flow.

Patch Changes

  • #12696 a2b22d0 - Apply the Agent Manager base branch picker selection to the active diff immediately. Changing the base branch now refreshes the diff against the new base instead of keeping the previous comparison until the scope or session changed.

  • #12720 57a9a60 - Fix Agent Manager embedded terminals not opening in the side panel or as a tab.

  • #12691 301c14e - Make Cmd/Ctrl+/ toggle the Agent Manager terminal even when the webview keybinding forwarding drops the key while the prompt input is focused, and stop it from triggering the Agent Manager terminal while the Kilo sidebar is focused.

  • #12694 af6bb00 - Match the Agent Manager terminal shortcut fallback to the platform modifier (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) and consume the extension echo once per keypress so unrelated invocations are no longer swallowed.

  • #12722 5678c09 - Fix the Agent Manager detail pane blanking when an unassigned session is selected. Clicking a session that belongs to no worktree now renders the chat and read-only banner again instead of an empty content area, and live terminal tabs stay mounted across the switch.

  • #12658 dbcd582 - Keep the Agent Manager terminal cursor visible on the bottom row.

  • #12369 44f1373 - Allow users to enable web search for models from all providers through Kilo configuration, VS Code settings, and Kilo Console settings.

  • #12624 af4cb42 Thanks @Hardik180704! - Persist MCP server enable and disable changes from VS Code settings across window reloads.

  • #12656 f0d2c8f - Navigate long conversations from a compact prompt rail that loads earlier history as you scroll.

  • #12692 faf0236 - Fix the @ "Past chats" picker in Agent Manager showing only the current session's directory. It now lists previous sessions across the whole worktree family — the local workspace and every Agent Manager worktree — each labeled with its worktree name, matching the Agent Manager session search. Any listed session can be attached as context, including chats from other worktrees of the same repository.

items.html:
7.4.17

Minor Changes

  • #12631 3321216 - Show the ⌘1-9 (Ctrl+1-9 on Windows/Linux) shortcut badges on every Agent Manager sidebar card while the modifier key is held, making it easy to see which number jumps to which worktree before pressing it.

  • #12598 c6711fc - Let users open Agent Manager terminals in the VS Code terminal or an embedded side panel. The terminal button's dropdown picks the destination; the side panel shares the right-hand inspector with the diff view and keeps running in the background when hidden.

  • #12633 23039c0 - Support multiple Agent Manager side-panel terminals per context. The panel header is now a tab strip that reuses the main tab bar's terminal tabs: click to switch, drag to reorder, X to close a single terminal, and + to open another one. Terminal numbers fill gaps left by closed terminals, and tabs pick up the live title from the shell or running program (OSC escape codes), so a dev server or build names its own tab.

  • #12632 0d853df - Add a prompt navigator rail to the chat transcript. A thin rail of ticks on the left edge shows one tick per prompt you sent; hovering or focusing it expands a card listing those prompts with a short preview of the answer, and clicking jumps the transcript to that turn. It appears in the sidebar, Kilo editor tabs, the sub-agent viewer, and Agent Manager, and never changes the readable width of the chat.

Patch Changes

  • #12629 0a1c140 - Keep each Agent Manager panel's terminal destination consistent. A dropdown pick is now remembered per panel and no longer flips when another window rewrites the shared terminal destination setting, so the terminal shortcut keeps opening the terminal type that panel is actually using. The shortcut also no longer dead-ends on worktrees without an active session, and terminals left over from a reloaded webview are cleaned up instead of leaking.

  • #12587 16f8e7e - Keep conversations and workspace files unchanged when a checkpoint cannot be fully restored.

  • #12333 290a5af Thanks @IamCoder18! - Include basic-auth credentials in the Local and Network Console URLs printed by kilo console, so users on headless hosts (no DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY, SSH sessions, CI runners) can open the URL in a browser on another machine and reach the Console.

  • #12630 a7f972f - Open Agent Manager terminals faster and avoid delayed shell prompts.

  • #12560 65c5e9d - Update the visible agent mode when cycling modes in Kilo sidebars and pending session tabs.

  • #12561 44f5963 - Fix settings changes sometimes failing to save and apply in VS Code.

  • #12540 2da8949 Thanks @Githubguy132010! - Preserve parenthesized tilde expressions as literal text in rendered chat messages.

  • #12591 625d2b9 - Show prompt input toggle tooltips instantly on hover instead of after a delay.

  • #12460 51d8031 - Changes from opencode v1.17.5 to v1.17.9 upstream:

    • Core Bugfixes: Improved MCP server compatibility by declaring Kilo's supported client capabilities.
    • Core Bugfixes: Plugin client requests now reuse the active server instead of assuming the default local port.
    • Core Bugfixes: ACP shell tool calls now show the command and working directory from the start.
    • Core Bugfixes: Plugin-provided shell environment variables now apply to PTY sessions.
    • Core Bugfixes: OpenAI-compatible providers now accept MCP tool schemas that previously failed validation. (@jquense)
    • Core Bugfixes: Cloudflare AI Gateway now receives the configured API key correctly. (@keefetang)
    • Core Bugfixes: MCP tools without declared schema properties now work with providers that expect object properties.
    • Core Bugfixes: Long-running MCP tools now keep their timeout alive when they report progress. (@Nomadcxx)
    • Core Bugfixes: The MCP OAuth callback server now shuts down once authorization finishes or is cancelled.
    • Core Bugfixes: MCP tool failures now surface the server's error text instead of a generic failure.
    • Core Bugfixes: MCP OAuth error pages now escape provider error text correctly.
    • Core Bugfixes: Honor configured agent step limits by forcing a final text response instead of failing mid-run.
    • Core Bugfixes: Queue steering prompts before dismissing pending questions so the previous turn cannot resume first.
    • Core Bugfixes: Prevent local server credentials from leaking into spawned PTY processes.
    • Core Bugfixes: Fix Devstral model detection when provider IDs use different casing. (@Robin1987China)
    • Core Bugfixes: Pass configured custom headers to Copilot model requests.
    • Core Improvements: MCP servers can now receive the current workspace as a client root.
    • Core Improvements: Session timelines load much faster and avoid flicker or scroll jumps.
    • Core Improvements: Add high and max thinking variants for GLM-5.2 across supported providers. (@imranshaiedi-byte)
    • Core Improvements: Stop wrapping follow-up user messages in a steering reminder so prompt caching stays effective.
    • TUI Bugfixes: MCP debug now uses the SDK's latest protocol version.
    • TUI Bugfixes: Only show the background subagent shortcut when the server supports it.
    • UI Bugfixes: Render completed Mermaid blocks from diagram source instead of fenced Markdown.

  • #11984 26dac19 Thanks @sylwester-liljegren! - Mention @ file references in the chat input placeholder so users know they can add file mentions. Translated across all supported languages.

  • #12593 160b066 - Prevent the VS Code backend from eagerly starting native file watchers for every Agent Manager worktree.

  • #12123 3075d35 Thanks @mjnaderi

items.summary: New The app now runs on the OpenCode 2 engine (2.0.32), with its standard tools and system prompt. Claude Opus 5.5 is in the model picker in every project. Picking it sets up the project's sandbox and opens a Claude chat on that model (for now Claude also…
items.html:
New
  • The app now runs on the OpenCode 2 engine (2.0.32), with its standard tools and system prompt.
  • Claude Opus 5.5 is in the model picker in every project. Picking it sets up the project's sandbox and opens a Claude chat on that model (for now Claude also needs Docker or Podman on this computer). If your account doesn't have Claude yet, the app says so.
Improved
  • In a chat you can now switch to another model from the same provider. Picking a model from another provider offers to start a new chat with it, since a chat keeps one provider.
  • On a new install, switching from GPT 6 Astra to GPT 6.1 Sol in a chat works right away, without offering a new chat.
Fixed
  • When sending stalls and the app asks you to check the previous message, Stop now clears it so you can carry on without restarting.
  • A message the app refuses before it reaches a model (for example "start a new chat to use another model", an update needed, or the daily limit reached) no longer counts against your session.
  • Chats upload completely: their automatic title, sub-agent chats with their own messages, and compactions, including Compact context.
  • The Linux sandbox sets up again: setup no longer stops at "Checking this computer…", and sandbox chats run inside the box.
  • Picking a model from another provider in a started chat no longer leaves the chat stuck on it: the chat keeps its own model and can still compact.
  • Chats started before the update carry on in the new version: a new message in an older chat now gets an answer.

items.title: OmniRush v3.7.5
items.summary: New Computer use in Settings > General: see whether it is on (and why not, such as on macOS), turn it off for this computer, and turn on “Use my own screen” after a short confirm (off by default). When you ask for something on a screen (use my browser, click,…
items.html:
New
  • Computer use in Settings > General: see whether it is on (and why not, such as on macOS), turn it off for this computer, and turn on “Use my own screen” after a short confirm (off by default). When you ask for something on a screen (use my browser, click, open an app), a tip above the message box turns it on.
  • Side-by-side diffs show what each turn changed.
  • Quote a message, or the text you selected in it, into the message box to reply to it.
  • Models can be limited to the sandbox or to your own computer. A project only lists the models its mode allows, and a chat keeps one model: to use another model, start a new chat.
Improved
  • Windows updates download only the parts that changed, so they are much smaller.
  • The Simplified Chinese translation is complete.
  • Messages you send while the sandbox is still setting up wait and go out once it is ready.
  • In the sandbox, the agent installs missing tools (for example ffmpeg) itself instead of asking you to.
Fixed
  • A response cut off part way now fails cleanly instead of showing an error or an empty chat.
  • On a Mac, a sandbox whose connection stays down is restarted automatically instead of failing until you stop it by hand.
  • A sponsored card limited to once a day no longer hides the card in its other spot.

items.title: OmniRush v3.7.4
items.summary: New /btw asks a quick side question about the chat, while the agent works or when it is idle. The answer shows above the message box and is not added to the chat. More ways to make the app yours in Settings > Appearance: three new themes (Graphite, Paper and…
items.html:
New
  • /btw asks a quick side question about the chat, while the agent works or when it is idle. The answer shows above the message box and is not added to the chat.
  • More ways to make the app yours in Settings > Appearance: three new themes (Graphite, Paper and Nocturne), an accent colour of your choice on any theme, separate interface and code fonts, compact spacing, and your own corner radius and text size.
  • Wallpaper: put a picture of your own behind the workspace, dim it, and choose how see-through and blurred the panels over it are. Panels stay solid when your computer is set to reduce transparency.
Improved
  • Keep up to 20 custom themes, each with its own name, instead of one. Pick, edit, delete, share or import each of them.
  • The accent colour is checked for contrast: you see a warning and a nearby readable colour when buttons or focus rings would be hard to see.
  • The chat sidebar gives its height to your chats: new chat and search share a row, the occasional places are one row of icons, and a project shows 10 chats before Show more.
  • The agent handles small tasks with less overhead: it reads related files together, keeps a todo list only for longer work, and skips guides a simple change doesn't need.
Fixed
  • The app no longer keeps piling up memory when a window stops reading its updates (for example while it is frozen or suspended).

items.title: OmniRush v3.7.3
items.summary: New The sandbox now sets itself up: on macOS the app starts its own small Linux VM (no Docker or other app needed), on Windows a Set up button installs WSL 2 with one admin prompt and resumes after the restart, and on Linux an Allow button does the one-time…
items.html:
New
  • The sandbox now sets itself up: on macOS the app starts its own small Linux VM (no Docker or other app needed), on Windows a Set up button installs WSL 2 with one admin prompt and resumes after the restart, and on Linux an Allow button does the one-time permission step. Progress and clear next steps show in the chat.
  • Servers you start in the sandbox open on this computer at the same localhost port.
Improved
  • Opening a project starts its sandbox right away, and the image downloads in the background, so the first message waits less.
  • In the sandbox, node_modules, Python environments and build folders are the sandbox's own Linux copies on macOS and Windows, so your Mac or Windows builds are never overwritten.
  • The agent carries multi-step tasks through to the end instead of stopping to ask whether to continue.
Fixed
  • Sandbox: a box with a fuse overlay no longer hangs on package installs, and starting a box never writes outside it.

items.title: OmniRush v3.7.2
items.summary: New Long chats have a Load earlier messages button at the top. Improved Computer use works on a display of its own with its own cursor, so your mouse, keyboard and clipboard stay yours. Fixed Undo and revert no longer remove chat turns or file changes without…
items.html:
New
  • Long chats have a Load earlier messages button at the top.
Improved
  • Computer use works on a display of its own with its own cursor, so your mouse, keyboard and clipboard stay yours.
Fixed
  • Undo and revert no longer remove chat turns or file changes without asking. Undo works only from the chat itself and ignores a held key, Revert and Edit say what they will take back, and hidden messages go only after you confirm a send.

items.title: OmniRush v3.7.1
items.summary: New See a command's output in the chat, while it runs and when it is done. How your allowance works: a help page for your daily tokens and the Good session checklist. Settings > General > Storage > Free up space removes files older versions left behind.…
items.html:
New
  • See a command's output in the chat, while it runs and when it is done.
  • How your allowance works: a help page for your daily tokens and the Good session checklist.
  • Settings > General > Storage > Free up space removes files older versions left behind.
Improved
  • Windows: after an update installs when you quit, the app opens again on the new version, and its shortcuts stay in place.
  • The built-in browser keeps working when you switch away, and asks for approval the way computer use does.
  • Clearer browser sign-in card: using your existing sign-ins is optional.
  • The window and the message box fit on short screens.
  • A shorter notice for settings not loaded from a project's config, and the chat title is no longer covered in the header.
  • The run status note shows only when something needs you (waiting for an answer, a message not yet confirmed, a retry), not during routine work.
Fixed
  • Computer use: "Allow for this chat" now applies to that one chat only, and a Deny withdraws the app's approval everywhere it was given.
  • Computer use from the terminal: copy the CLI connection again in the desktop app (its file was renamed).
  • Windows: messages that mention a local file send again.
  • Library: opening an item and going back works again (the page no longer gets stuck).
  • A chat saved with a model that is no longer available switches to the default OmniRush model and says so, instead of leaving Send disabled.

items.title: OmniRush v3.7.0
items.summary: Fixed The Mac app starts again. Desktop 3.6.7 and 3.6.9 stopped on macOS with "The bundled engine was changed". Also in this release (from 3.6.9) Security: commands the agent runs no longer receive the app's own keys. Security: approvals, permission mode,…
items.html:
Fixed
  • The Mac app starts again. Desktop 3.6.7 and 3.6.9 stopped on macOS with "The bundled engine was changed".
Also in this release (from 3.6.9)
  • Security: commands the agent runs no longer receive the app's own keys.
  • Security: approvals, permission mode, project settings, plugins, MCP servers and keys can only be changed from the app's own window, not with a key read from disk.
  • Computer use: no approval on each step; one Allow per app per chat. In Normal mode it still asks before paying or buying and before typing a password.

items.title: OmniRush v3.6.7
items.summary: Security A project's MCP settings can no longer hand the app's keys or files outside the project to an MCP server, and no local MCP server starts unless the app's checks are running. Better masking of access keys that tools print with escaped characters. New…
items.html:
Security
  • A project's MCP settings can no longer hand the app's keys or files outside the project to an MCP server, and no local MCP server starts unless the app's checks are running.
  • Better masking of access keys that tools print with escaped characters.
New
  • What's new: see what changed in each release from the sidebar, the Help menu or the command palette, and a short note after each update.
  • Themes: eight presets with light and dark versions, and your own theme in Settings › Appearance with a live preview and contrast checks. Share it as a code or a file; the editor, terminal and chat all follow it.
  • Computer use: the agent can operate an app window you approve (screenshots, clicks, typing), with a stop control and approvals that follow your permission mode. Off until it is enabled for your account.
  • Editor: search, problems and language features, a split editor, editor settings, Markdown and image preview, and a Git change gutter. Format on save asks once before running a project's own formatter.
Improved
  • Only OmniRush models are offered. Other providers, and your own opencode plugins and custom tools, stay off.
  • Fewer repeated failed edits: when an edit can't find its text, the agent now sees the file's current lines.
  • The reasoning effort shown in the model picker is always the one used.
  • The session quality status now sits inside its chip instead of above the chat.

items.html:
Security

  • A project's own plugins, language servers and formatters are no longer loaded from its configuration.
  • MCP servers start through the system's own npx and uvx, never a copy inside the project.

Added

  • Permission modes: Careful asks before every file change and command, Normal (the default) asks only before risky actions, Auto never asks.
  • A notification when a task finishes or waits for your approval.
  • Chat and IDE layouts.
  • Figma designs through a supported MCP server.

Fixed

  • Session sharing is turned off; it used an outside service that has shut down.
  • A calmer start screen: the greeting and the composer, with your recent chats in one line below it.
  • Long answers are kept in sync while they run.
  • The handoff question is asked once per chat, only when the chat is idle; a failed handoff can be retried.
  • Undo keeps your editor saves and refreshes open files.
  • Skills you added are kept when you update.
  • The approval buttons fit in a narrow chat.

items.html:

  • MCP servers defined in a project's own configuration no longer start on their own. Only supported servers start, at a supported version, working inside the project; others are listed with the reason they were skipped.

Added

  • A code editor beside the chat.
  • Review your changes and fix what the review found; undo the last turn while keeping your own later edits, and redo it; see the chat's changes and status.
  • Parallel tasks, each in its own copy of the project, and a home screen with recent projects and chats and a search of past chats.
  • The agent checks its own changes with the project's checks, keeps project notes in AGENTS.md, sees code diagnostics after edits, and writes fuller summaries when a long chat is compacted. Each can be switched off in Settings.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.11
items.summary: This release improves Git authentication, Windows compatibility, and SSH responsiveness. It also reduces background fetch overhead, fixes pane shortcuts after switching tasks, and adds an in-app signup for Emdash 2.0 early access. Highlights The project's Git…
items.html:
This release improves Git authentication, Windows compatibility, and SSH responsiveness. It also reduces background fetch overhead, fixes pane shortcuts after switching tasks, and adds an in-app signup for Emdash 2.0 early access.

Highlights
  • The project's Git credentials setting now applies to Emdash's own local Git operations, including push, pull, and fetch. Choosing System uses the machine's credentials, while an account explicitly selected for an operation still takes precedence.
  • Join the Emdash 2.0 waitlist directly from the sidebar, with your email and an optional note about your team or workflow. The card can be dismissed for the current release.
Fixes
  • Commit & Push and other Git network operations on Windows authenticate correctly through the connected account, fixing failures where pushing from a terminal worked but pushing from Emdash did not.
  • Agent hooks on Windows run correctly when launched through Git Bash, including Claude Code hooks. Prompt and assistant text passed to hooks is no longer misinterpreted as shell commands.
  • Windows builds resolve the bundled SSH dependency correctly, fixing a module-loading error reported in v1.2.10.
  • SSH connections send handshake and interactive traffic without waiting for TCP buffering, improving responsiveness when connecting to and working on remote machines.
  • Background Git fetches wait after the previous fetch finishes and back off when a repository is slow. Fetches also avoid unnecessary metadata writes and automatic maintenance, reducing disk work and contention with other Git operations.
  • Self-hosted Git integrations correctly match remotes that use custom HTTP or HTTPS ports, including Forgejo instances.
  • Pane shortcuts remain active after switching tasks or projects when a terminal or input has already received focus.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.10
items.summary: This release lets you trust repositories that Git refuses because of their ownership, stops background processes from opening console windows on Windows, and keeps large repositories responsive. It also fixes Clean Artifacts, Git SSH configuration, credential…
items.html:
This release lets you trust repositories that Git refuses because of their ownership, stops background processes from opening console windows on Windows, and keeps large repositories responsive. It also fixes Clean Artifacts, Git SSH configuration, credential handling, and panel sizes. Remote machines get these fixes once you update their workspace server in Settings > Machines.

Highlights
  • When Git refuses a repository because another user owns it, such as a repository in a WSL folder, Add Project explains why and shows the Git command to run yourself. Trust Repository adds that one folder to your global Git configuration after confirmation, which also applies to agents and terminals. For SSH projects, the entry is written on the remote machine.
  • On Windows, Git, agents, SSH connections, and other background processes no longer open console windows or Windows Terminal tabs.
  • Changed-file diffs load while background Git work runs and show a loading state or error instead of a blank pane. If a reload fails, the last loaded diff stays visible and read-only until it recovers.
  • The Workspaces tab measures disk usage much faster, counts worktrees inside their repository only once, reuses results for five minutes, and stops scanning when you leave the view.
  • Creating tasks on large repositories, re-provisioning, deleting tasks and workspaces, updating pull request checkouts, and other long-running workspace operations no longer fail after 30 seconds while the machine is still working on them.
Fixes
  • Clean Artifacts in the Workspaces tab removes ignored build output in place instead of removing the worktree. Tracked files, uncommitted and untracked changes, local .env files, files matching your preserve patterns, nested workspaces, and linked tasks all stay. Emdash won't clean a workspace while agents or terminals are running in it, and the action is available for local workspaces.
  • Clones and other Git operations use the core.sshCommand from your Git configuration, so SSH key routers and per-host keys work.
  • Git credential requests bypass proxy settings. When a credential read fails, for example in a tmux session reattached after Emdash restarted, Git prints the reason before prompting.
  • New tmux tasks get their own environment and no longer inherit stale variables or credentials from earlier sessions. Credential tokens and environment values stay out of process arguments, where other users on a shared machine could read them.
  • Creating a worktree recovers from worktrees deleted outside Emdash without running git worktree prune by hand. Git failures show Git's message instead of a bare exit code, with credential URLs and tokens removed. Deleting a worktree whose branch is already gone succeeds.
  • The sidebars and terminal drawer keep the size you set when the window resizes, including when a tiling window manager rearranges windows, and return to it after a small window grows again.
  • When the default branch can't be resolved, Create Task explains that you need to select a branch in workspace settings. Automations show the same reason, and changing an automation's schedule saves only the schedule.
  • On Linux and Windows with Watchman running, Emdash watches Git metadata with the system file watcher, so Watchman no longer crawls the .git directory.
  • Agents on Windows no longer create a stray %SystemDrive%\ProgramData folder tree in their working directory, and they receive the system and program folder variables that .NET and NuGet need.
  • The Linux .deb and .rpm packages declare ALSA and GBM as dependencies, so the app starts on minimal installs.
  • Crash-loop recovery shows why the most recent launch failed.
  • Stored notifications are trimmed to the newest 500 on launch, as intended.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.9
items.summary: This release adds GitLab repository and merge request workflows, with browser and device sign-in for GitLab.com. It also adds support for Apple silicon Mac remotes and improves terminal links, account reconnection, and project dialogs. Highlights Create GitLab…
items.html:
This release adds GitLab repository and merge request workflows, with browser and device sign-in for GitLab.com. It also adds support for Apple silicon Mac remotes and improves terminal links, account reconnection, and project dialogs.

Highlights
  • Create GitLab repositories in personal namespaces or existing groups, including nested groups, and publish an existing project through Add Remote. Connected self-hosted instances are supported, and task creation uses GitLab's work-item terminology.
  • Browse, create, and merge GitLab merge requests from Emdash. View approvals, pipeline jobs, discussions, commits, and changed files, mark drafts ready, and start or review tasks from merge requests, including those from forks.
  • Connect GitLab.com through your Emdash account or with a device code, with automatic token renewal. Device sign-in stays inside the connection dialog with copy, open, retry, and cancel controls. Self-hosted GitLab instances continue to use access tokens.
  • Remote workspace server installation now supports Apple silicon Macs using the tools included with macOS. Terminal sessions on those hosts start correctly after installation.
Fixes
  • Wrapped terminal hyperlinks open their full destination, including links printed by Claude Code. Copy Link uses the hyperlink's destination or joins lines wrapped by the terminal, while normal selection copying preserves line breaks and keeps separate URLs apart.
  • Clicking a terminal hyperlink opens it locally without also asking the remote agent to launch a browser. Link handling preserves text selection and cancels pending clicks when dragging or switching focus. IPv6 URLs retain their closing brackets.
  • Long directory paths stay within project dialogs, keeping the directory chooser visible at narrow window widths.
  • Add Remote creates an empty repository before publishing the current branch, preserving existing history. Repository creation, fetching, and publishing consistently use the selected account.
  • Creating a task from a branch opens the workspace settings directly, with no issue or merge request preselected.
  • GitLab merge request reviews recover missing commits from the correct source, including fork merge requests. Refreshing the merge request list retains cached details, and unavailable diff counts remain unknown instead of appearing as zero.
  • Expiring integration credentials renew before Git operations use them. Tokens replaced on another device are refreshed after rejection, and temporary renewal failures can be retried.
  • Reconnecting preserves the selected account, and background token renewal cannot restore a disconnected account or overwrite a newer connection. Cancelled device sign-in saves nothing, and newly issued tokens are retried if the provider briefly rejects them.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.8
items.summary: This release adds language intelligence to the editor, subscription usage meters, and YouTrack integration. It also brings diff comments to chat and improves file browsing, agent status, and desktop integration. Highlights The editor adds hover information,…
items.html:
This release adds language intelligence to the editor, subscription usage meters, and YouTrack integration. It also brings diff comments to chat and improves file browsing, agent status, and desktop integration.

Highlights
  • The editor adds hover information, definitions, type definitions, references, and diagnostics for local and SSH workspaces. JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python language servers are bundled; additional servers support Bash, Go, Rust, C/C++, JSON, YAML, HTML, and CSS dialects. Language service status and restart controls are available in the file tab menu.
  • A new Usage page in settings shows remaining Codex and Claude Code subscription allowances, reset countdowns, and refresh controls. Shared accounts appear once across machines, and stale or unavailable readings are clearly marked.
  • Connect YouTrack Cloud or self-hosted instances with a permanent token, search tickets using YouTrack queries, and start tasks with ticket descriptions and comments. Ticket context includes up to the latest 100 accessible comments and uses readable ticket identifiers.
  • Attach draft diff comments to chat through the “Diff comments” item in the @ menu. Comments are cleared only after confirmed delivery, while failed sends and comments edited during submission remain pending.
  • Jira setup now offers a choice between email and API token or a manually supplied bearer access token.
  • Branch Commits can switch between a flat file list and a nested tree, with its own saved view preference.
Fixes
  • File browsing shares live folder listings across views and updates changed folders without rebuilding the entire tree. Folder expansion, drag-hover, and new-file placement are more reliable, names sort naturally, and files named __proto__ remain visible and editable.
  • Language services preserve unsaved edits across restarts and reconnects. Built-in editor support remains available where supported when a language server is unavailable, and language service or usage worker failures no longer block host startup.
  • Switching back to a task keeps terminal and agent dimensions in sync, preventing misplaced cursors, clipped lines, and overdrawn frames. Hidden panes no longer produce invalid terminal grid sizes.
  • Cursor and OpenCode working indicators clear correctly when agents finish or stop, including OpenCode sessions using custom providers. Chat resumes its working indicator after permission approval and ignores late prompt results after a session closes.
  • Chat preserves prices, literal HTML and XML, and inline math source instead of hiding text or showing empty message cards. Claude monitor events appear as passive notifications without interrupting active turns or duplicating screen-reader output.
  • Hidden issue and review context stays out of replayed chat transcripts. Draft diff comments remain visible when switching files or when the editor finishes loading.
  • SSH connections support OpenSSH user certificates supplied by the SSH agent. Reconnection logs include the underlying error instead of an unreadable object value.
  • Installed-app detection on macOS avoids application chooser prompts and recognizes GUI-only apps. Failed checks can be retried, and Windows detection respects custom installation directories.
  • Opening remote workspaces in VS Code, VSCodium, or Cursor requests a new window. “Open in Terminal” on Linux tries the user's default terminal before falling back to common terminal applications.
  • Merge commits show files changed against their first parent. Project and workspace inspection preserve Git errors instead of treating failed repository checks as ordinary directories.
  • Agent installation shows all supported options for the current platform, including WinGet for Claude Code on Windows.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.7
items.summary: This release remembers agent settings across tasks, adds native provider controls to the chat composer, and improves session recovery. It also makes update downloads, project opening, and conversation navigation more reliable. Highlights Chat remembers your…
items.html:
This release remembers agent settings across tasks, adds native provider controls to the chat composer, and improves session recovery. It also makes update downloads, project opening, and conversation navigation more reliable.

Highlights
  • Chat remembers your model, effort, access mode, and other provider settings across tasks and projects, with separate preferences for each agent and machine. New automations inherit these preferences and retain their own saved settings for scheduled runs.
  • Switch between Chat UI and TUI directly in the agent selector. Your interface choice is remembered across agents, projects, and machines.
  • Task creation and active chat use the provider's available configuration options, including a fast-mode toggle where supported. Chat permissions follow the provider's native access mode, and TUI auto-approval is remembered separately.
  • Claude's model picker adds Opus 5.5, and Codex adds GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Model choices use the identifiers supported by each agent so selections carry through to the session correctly.
Fixes
  • Missing ACP sessions can be retried or replaced with a fresh session in the same conversation, preserving drafts and selected settings. Sessions that never started recover automatically when the provider confirms they are missing.
  • Initial prompts survive failed startup preparation and worker restarts. Transcripts remain visible while sessions reconnect and reload their history.
  • Cached composer settings remain visible during startup, and failed preference saves show a warning. Changing shared preferences leaves existing conversations and saved automations unchanged.
  • Notification clicks focus or reopen the correct conversation tab, including chats in another pane, without creating a blank terminal tab.
  • Update downloads keep their progress when navigating away from settings or when a request times out. Failures show readable messages, retry controls, and expandable diagnostics that can be copied with credentials redacted.
  • Agent discovery avoids repeated checks, and local project opening retries temporary timeouts. Cancelled or failed initialization cleans up background work without interrupting existing task sessions.
  • Imports from v0 preserve workspace paths, remote conversation locations, and valid Claude session resume information.
  • File links in chat open the editor at the referenced line number.
  • POSIX paths retain forward-slash separators and preserve literal backslashes in filenames.
  • CSV previews retain an empty quoted row at the end of a file, even without a trailing newline.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.6
items.summary: This release restores file drops and image pastes in remote terminals, adds OpenCode v2 status support, and detects IPv6 preview servers. It also improves search results, agent session restoration, and desktop integration. Highlights Drop local files or paste…
items.html:
This release restores file drops and image pastes in remote terminals, adds OpenCode v2 status support, and detects IPv6 preview servers. It also improves search results, agent session restoration, and desktop integration.

Highlights
  • Drop local files or paste images into remote agent terminals and shells. Files upload to the machine running the session before their paths are inserted, with progress and error feedback.
  • OpenCode v2 reports working, completion, and error status through native hooks. Interrupted runs return to idle, and session tracking remains compatible with earlier OpenCode versions.
  • Preview detection recognizes IPv6 loopback URLs such as http://[::1]:3000, with correctly formatted links in the preview server list.
Fixes
  • File drops into Claude Code terminals retain the full path instead of leaving only a space. Image pastes avoid duplicate attachments, and pending transfers are cancelled when their target pane or session changes.
  • Stored attachments remain available across session shutdowns, workspace deactivation, and restarts without expiring by age. Incomplete uploads are cleaned up after crashes, and deleting a conversation or workspace also cleans up its stored attachments.
  • Antigravity resumes the correct native conversation instead of starting a fresh session with a “conversation not found” warning.
  • Search removes duplicate and stale results for projects, tasks, and conversations. Deleting a project also removes its tasks and conversations from search.
  • Commit file lists and working-tree diffs preserve filenames containing Unicode, quotes, tabs, or other special characters, including renamed and copied files.
  • The in-app browser keeps a successfully loaded page visible when an embedded iframe fails to load.
  • Remote workspace creation retries failed home-directory lookups after a host reconnects, avoiding persistent “unusable runtime” errors.
  • macOS Option-arrow shortcuts retain their native behavior in terminal agents while shell panes keep word navigation.
  • Linux launcher and window identities match correctly on Wayland and X11, keeping dock grouping consistent and preserving existing pins for stable and canary builds.
  • Agent settings and the agent selector show installation guide links, and link icons are placed consistently.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.5
items.summary: This release adds multiple accounts per integration, custom agent executable selection, and more control over the workbench. It also makes ACP conversations, task archiving, and remote connections more reliable. Highlights Connect multiple accounts for each…
items.html:
This release adds multiple accounts per integration, custom agent executable selection, and more control over the workbench. It also makes ACP conversations, task archiving, and remote connections more reliable.

Highlights
  • Connect multiple accounts for each integration, choose a default, and select which account each project uses. Account choices carry through project creation, issue browsing, and pull request workflows.
  • Choose an agent executable by path or command name in settings, validate it before saving, and use that selection when launching agents. Custom wrapper scripts are supported, including PowerShell wrappers on Windows.
  • Hide the Emdash menu bar or system tray icon from Interface settings.
  • Newly opened file diffs scroll directly to the first change, while previously viewed diffs retain their saved position.
  • Codex adds a curl installation option on macOS and Linux, and MCP startup failures appear in the chat composer's server list with error details.
Fixes
  • ACP transcripts keep pending prompts and live responses visible as turns finish and history loads. Scroll position and session settings survive history refreshes, and background agent events update the correct turn.
  • Failed session restores preserve saved conversations and show recoverable errors. Agent sign-in remains accessible, and terminal startup failures no longer disrupt the ACP worker.
  • Each conversation retains its prompt draft, text selection, undo history, and composer scroll position when switching tabs. Empty chats keep the composer centered during startup.
  • Archiving runs teardown scripts when possible and remains available when a remote host is offline. Restoring archived tasks works across repeated archive and restore cycles, and cleanup state stays consistent across restarts.
  • Workspace lookup uses current saved state, avoiding stale “workspace not found” errors. Conversation lists recover after missed updates, and closing a conversation tab clears its attention indicator.
  • Pull request details refresh reliably after runtime recovery, and CI results stay tied to the current commit. Staged and unstaged file lists remain stable during background Git updates.
  • SSH-config connections allow authentication and private key overrides. Testing and saving use the same credentials, and saved passwords and passphrases are reused only for the matching connection or key.
  • Routine remote connection checks no longer cause status flicker or interrupt terminal input. Git credentials also remain available to child processes, including editor extensions.
  • Muse Code and Antigravity report working and completion status through native hooks. Codex approval settings parse correctly on Windows, and Devin handles compound shell commands correctly.
  • macOS Option-arrow shortcuts navigate shell words correctly, and tmux startup handles terminal capability queries more reliably.
  • Localhost links offer the usual choice to open in Emdash or an external browser. Pane focus preserves scroll position, sidebar task reordering stays accurate after auto-scroll, and panels remain clickable over the title bar.
  • Project opening failures show actionable errors, including invalid remote default branches. Crash recovery also offers an explicit option to reset saved UI state and reload.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.4
items.summary: This release makes ACP conversations easier to follow and more reliable to use, especially across remote reconnections. It also adds Muse Code, project renaming, and several agent and provider improvements. Highlights Agent activity is easier to scan: related…
items.html:
This release makes ACP conversations easier to follow and more reliable to use, especially across remote reconnections. It also adds Muse Code, project renaming, and several agent and provider improvements.

Highlights
  • Agent activity is easier to scan: related thinking blocks are grouped, consecutive tool calls collapse into “Ran N commands,” and command rows use compact, descriptive headings.
  • Rename projects directly from the project header or sidebar menu.
  • Muse Code is now available as a coding agent, and CodeBuddy Code adds lifecycle hooks for accurate status, session, error, and permission notifications.
  • Codex adds GPT-6 Astra to its model options, and OpenCode can connect to OrcaRouter as a named OpenAI-compatible provider.
  • The chat composer now shows the selected model effort beside the model name.
Fixes
  • Prompt queuing works correctly while an ACP agent is active. Drafts are preserved across tab changes and delivery failures, and prompts clear only after the agent accepts them.
  • Remote projects and conversations recover more reliably after sleep, network interruptions, and workspace-server reconnects. Transcript history reloads correctly, and connection status remains stable during recovery.
  • Terminal and TUI-agent sessions use readable, identity-backed tmux names and recover the correct process more reliably, including after idle periods.
  • Pull request status refreshes consistently, repositories are polled every minute, and requested or startup-failed CI checks are classified correctly.
  • External symlink targets can be browsed in the file tree, while diff buffers remain read-only and file references from agent transcripts open at the reported line.
  • SSH connections respect filtered agent identities, and macOS can request local-network access when connecting to machines over LAN SSH.
  • Project migrations handle legacy workspace identity conflicts without interrupting registry sync.
  • The in-app browser favicon, external-link dialog, task-tab cursor, collapsed plans, and prompt-editor links now behave consistently.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.3
items.summary: This release adds Prime Agent, project-level environment variables, drag-to-split panes, and native Linux ARM64 builds. It also refreshes the workbench and file tree while improving file watching, search, and restored sessions. Highlights Prime Agent is now…
items.html:
This release adds Prime Agent, project-level environment variables, drag-to-split panes, and native Linux ARM64 builds. It also refreshes the workbench and file tree while improving file watching, search, and restored sessions.

Highlights
  • Prime Agent is now available as a coding agent, with native ACP chat, resumable sessions, MCP servers, and Emdash hooks.
  • Define environment variables in project settings and apply them consistently to agents, terminals, and lifecycle scripts.
  • Drag a tab to any edge of a pane to create a split and place it there. Tab bars and the terminal drawer also have a cleaner, flatter design.
  • The file explorer now carries Git status colors up to parent folders, making changed files easier to locate.
  • Claude adds Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 support.
  • Native Linux packages are now built for both x64 and ARM64 in AppImage, DEB, and RPM formats.
Fixes
  • File search and file watching recover more reliably from failed or cancelled watchers, honor exclusion settings, and avoid holding inactive workspaces open.
  • Git repositories remain usable if a watcher cannot attach, and repository scans do less redundant work.
  • Restored terminal-agent sessions recover correctly after an app restart.
  • Markdown reference links and images render correctly, and wide tables can scroll horizontally.
  • The chat composer keeps the caret visible across line breaks, while mention and other selection popovers stay within the viewport.
  • Project directory browsing, task-specific sidebar widths, terminal theme changes, and empty terminal drawers now behave consistently.
  • Linux secure storage is configured before startup, and Windows agent launching prefers the correct executable shim.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.2

items.html:
This release adds Plan mode to Codex chat and improves remote development over Tailscale SSH, along with more reliable agent launching on Windows.

Highlights
  • Codex ACP conversations can switch between Default and Plan modes directly from the chat composer, with the selection remembered across sessions.
Fixes
  • Remote workspaces can connect over Tailscale SSH now that Unix socket forwarding works with compatible servers that use a non-OpenSSH identification banner.
  • Windows preserves native command lines when launching .cmd agent shims, so agents such as Pi start correctly when arguments contain spaces or quotes.
  • Saved ACP configuration options are cleared when an agent no longer supports them, preventing stale selections from being reapplied.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.1

items.html:
This small release focuses on reliability across remote development, Windows, and agent sessions.

Fixes
  • Remote ACP prompts no longer time out while an agent is working, and successfully delivered prompts no longer show a false failure or return to the composer.
  • Large prompts and dropped files are stored on the target machine so remote agents can access them reliably.
  • Windows project activation now handles drive-letter and UNC paths, with more reliable agent launching, shell detection, and process cleanup.
  • Workspace, worktree, and file paths are handled consistently on Windows, including directory selection, file opening, links, and symlinks.
  • The remote project directory picker stays responsive and no longer repeats loading cycles while navigating.
  • Project settings are preserved through transient read failures, and worktrees are no longer modified with Emdash-specific state.

items.title: Emdash v1.2.0
items.summary: This release introduces the new Emdash Workspace Server, bringing remote development much closer to the local Emdash experience. It also adds per-machine management for agent resources, file-content search, faster task creation, and a more capable and reliable…
items.html:
This release introduces the new Emdash Workspace Server, bringing remote development much closer to the local Emdash experience. It also adds per-machine management for agent resources, file-content search, faster task creation, and a more capable and reliable chat UI for ACP agents.

Highlights
  • The Emdash Workspace Server brings remote projects on par with local development, including Git, files, terminals, agents, automations, file search, and preview forwarding.
  • Manage each machine independently, including its workspaces, conversations, agents, MCP servers, skills, dependencies, and resource usage.
  • Search file contents from the task sidebar with Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F, jump directly to matching lines, and automatically reveal opened files in the file tree.
  • Tasks open faster, with non-blocking setup work continuing in the background. A new Activity menu shows worktree setup and lifecycle-script progress.
  • The ACP chat UI now keeps drafts and attachments across navigation and delivery failures, restores suspended conversations without disrupting chat, and remembers provider and session options.
Everything else
  • Open an existing workspace in a task instead of creating a new worktree.
  • Sort project tasks by last used or creation time.
  • Rename conversations and select multiple conversations for deletion.
  • The command palette now searches commands, files, conversations, projects, and tasks, while Settings has its own searchable navigation.
  • CodeBuddy is available as a coding agent, Claude adds Opus 5 while retaining Opus 4.8, and agent selectors show clearer capability icons.
  • PhpStorm is available in the Open In menu.
  • Project settings show where a new worktree will be created, and long lists such as Git remotes are searchable.
  • The app shows its window and branded loading state sooner, includes better startup recovery, and adds a system tray icon.
  • Project expansion preferences persist across restarts, and expanded projects use the open-folder icon.
Fixes
  • Pull request detection stays stable across refreshes and matches the exact head branch; staging remains responsive, diff paths stay checkout-relative, and branch commits no longer flicker.
  • Editor and diff scroll positions survive tab and task switches, the commit input no longer steals focus, and file reveal operations no longer time out during tree refreshes.
  • Chat execution text no longer clips, search labels are no longer duplicated, raw search queries are preserved, and file links open in the adjacent editor pane.
  • Sidebar shortcuts expand collapsed panels and keep working through overlays; the theme command is restored to the command palette.
  • New-task settings and GitHub identity details fit correctly in the modal, and auto-approve preferences persist.
  • Remote projects behave more reliably across reconnects and relinks, recover failed file watchers, and publish branches to the correct remote.
  • Terminal processes receive the user's environment without leaking worker settings, and terminal QR codes render without line gaps.
  • Windows title bars follow the app theme, and agent hooks work correctly on Windows.
  • Codex notifications and device authentication work again, and provider environment variables are applied correctly to ACP sessions.
  • Automation controls, project and settings layouts, markdown checkbox contrast, and other interface details have been polished.

Emdash v1.1.27 is out! Emdash v1.1.25 is out! Emdash v1.1.24 is out!

This release brings major improvements to SSH and remote workflows (including ProxyJump, ProxyCommand, ForwardAgent, and better MaxSessions handling), a more polished navigation and sidebar experience, better task and PR flows, expanded terminal/open-in-app support, new integrations and providers (Neon, Antigravity, Asana polish), plus a long list of stability, performance, editor, and UI fixes across the app.

Emdash v1.1.19 is out! This release includes smoother SSH and remote project workflows, improvements to navigation and the command palette, better PR/diff tooling (including richer file list info and PR comment rendering), new integrations and providers (Asana, Linear updates, Grok CLI), plus a long list of stability, performance, and terminal fixes across platforms.

Emdash v1.1.10 is out!

This release brings new editor and terminal integrations (Kitty, Android Studio, VSCodium, Junie CLI, opencode), improved diff editing, a command palette, and a batch of reliability fixes across Git, SSH, and Windows - plus contributions from the community.

items.html:
Emdash v1.1.5

Emdash v1 is now stable.

This release builds on the v1 launch with a set of fixes, performance improvements, and groundwork for upcoming features like remote workflows and BYOI workspaces.

If you're upgrading from v0.4.x, you can import your existing tasks during onboarding.

items.html:
@oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core

Changed
  • prepareCompaction() runs as the compaction.prepare loop phase, so a ui.loop-blocked stall from a cold token walk over a long branch names compaction instead of "unknown" (#15027, #18867 by @wolfiesch)

@oh-my-pi/pi-ai

Added
  • Added the google-decisions judgment API for Google's Gemini Decisions API (gemini-decision-1), with text and image input (#19060 by @kevcube)
  • Added apiKey to successful OAuthAccessResolution results from oauth.accessById() and oauth.accessAll(): the key normal requests send for that account, which differs from accessToken for providers with structured credentials (#19030 by @Xytronix)
  • Added an optional exemptionAlias to ToolCallLoopGuard so transport calls can match the dispatched tool's name in exemptTools (#18860)
  • Added the liquid-systemone judgment API for Liquid AI's decision models, which rejects image sets over Liquid's 10,000 32×32-patch request cap before sending (#18076, #18100 by @SuperUserA)
  • Added the nace-systemone judgment API for Nace's Drex decision models, which sends images as Drex's top-level images data URLs and replaces the base64 image, audio, video and PDF data URLs that Drex rejects in judged text with a description (#18950 by @alphastorm)
Fixed
  • Fixed a spent Codex account retrying every minute for days when its siblings were only refused the requested model: their short model-policy blocks no longer count as a sibling becoming available, so the usage-limit wait follows the spent account's reset and model fallback can take over (#17637, #19019 by @wolfiesch)
  • Auth-gateway client tokens (serve --clients) can no longer set who a request is from, who pays, or how the gateway reaches the provider: chat routes drop their request headers, userProfileId, initiatorOverride, metadata, serviceTier, cacheRetention and the other gateway-only options, while the gateway token keeps them (#19067 by @alphastorm)
  • Fixed the auth gateway's /v1/pi/stream dropping taskBudget, include and anthropicPrefixMismatchBehavior, which its other chat routes accept (#19067 by @alphastorm)
  • Fixed requests to Vertex AI Mistral partner models (mistral-medium-3, mistral-small-2503, codestral-2) failing because they were sent in Anthropic's request format (#19010, #19022 by @yuzu-octopus)
  • Added Gemini's xhigh thinking level, sent on the Gemini API and Vertex for models whose ladder exposes it (Gemini 4 Hydrogen).
  • Fixed omp failing to start with ENOTDIR: not a directory, stat '~/.aws/credentials' when ~/.aws is a file instead of a directory (#19083 by @iamshatter)

@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog

Added
  • Added the Gemini Decision 1 judge model (google/gemini-decision-1, GEMINI_API_KEY); assign it to the judge role to use it (#19060 by @kevcube)
  • Added Nace (nace) with the drex-max-v1.1, drex-max-finance and drex-v2.0 judge models and /login nace (NACE_API_KEY) (#18950 by @alphastorm)
  • Added Gemini 4 Hydrogen (gemini-4-hydrogen) on Google, Vertex, OpenCode Zen, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, and Kilo, with low, medium, high, and xhigh thinking levels on the native Google transports.
Changed
  • Factory Droid requests identify as droid 1.7.1 and report the interactive CLI as their surface, and prefix-bound Claude models (Opus, Sonnet and Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.1) on Factory's direct Anthropic route now ask Anthropic to drop stale signed thinking instead of rejecting a turn whose earlier context changed (#18771 by @will-bogusz)
Fixed
  • Fixed alibaba-token-plan/qwen4-max-preview (including its qwen4.0-max-preview alias) showing no context or output limits, image input, or thinking levels (#18986).
  • Fixed Vertex AI Mistral partner models (mistral-medium-3, mistral-small-2503, codestral-2) misrouting to the first-party Gemini endpoint; they now ride the publishers/mistralai raw-predict endpoint with ADC auth and an OpenAI-shaped body (#19010, #19022 by @yuzu-octopus).
  • Added Liquid AI (liquid) with the d1.1 and d1-ultra judge models and /login liquid (LIQUID_API_KEY) (#18076, #18100 by @SuperUserA)

@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent

Breaking Changes
  • secrets.yml regex rules are now Rust regex patterns run natively, in linear time: lookarounds and backreferences are no longer supported, and a (?P<secret>…) group marks the part to redact (text around it is context that stays); \d, \w and \s are Unicode-aware. A regex rule that does not compile stops startup with an error naming the file and entry instead of being skipped. Migrate (?<=password=)\S+ to password=(?P<secret>\S+); see docs/secrets.md (#18965 by @H4vC)
  • Secret placeholders are now four camelCased words after the friendly name, e.g. GitHubToken_correctHorseStapleBattery, with no $$ delimiters, and the transcript shows the real value wherever the model wrote one. Placeholders in the old $$NAME_HASH:CASE$$ form, in sessions saved before this change, stay literal text, including in tool calls the model copies them into; start a new session to get working placeholders (#19014 by @H4vC)
  • What the model writes from placeholders (replies, thinking, tool calls, summaries) is stored as written and replayed byte-identical, keeping thinking signatures and prompt caches valid; model output that still holds a value (written while redaction was off, or before the secret was configured) is redacted on replay. Values a regex rule finds later no longer rewrite earlier history. A friendlyName
